title: New Ghost Shark Species Discovered Near Costa Rica
content:
Costa Rican scientists have reported the possible discovery of a new species of ghost shark (family Dalatiidae) in the Pacific waters off Cabo Blanco and Cano Island. The specimen was collected during a routine survey by the National Institute of Biodiversity and Ecosystem Conservation and exhibits distinct morphological features that differ from known ghost shark species, prompting preliminary classification as *Dalatias* sp. nov.

The team, led by marine biologist Dr. Ana Morales, noted that the shark’s body shape, fin placement, and dermal denticle pattern are unlike those of the common *Dalatias licha*, the only other ghost shark recorded in the region. Genetic analysis of tissue samples is underway to confirm the taxonomic status, while researchers plan additional dives to assess the population size and habitat preferences of the putative new species. This finding adds to the growing recognition of the Pacific coast of Costa Rica as a biodiversity hotspot for elasmobranchs.

If confirmed, the discovery would expand scientific knowledge of deep‑water shark diversity and underscore the importance of protecting the marine ecosystems surrounding Cabo Blanco and Cano Island. The research team will publish their full findings in a peer‑reviewed journal later this year, providing a foundation for future conservation and management strategies in the area.

title: Ancient Yeast Found in Iceman's Remains
content:
Scientists have discovered that a species of yeast has survived for more than five thousand years in the gut of the famed frozen mummy known as Ötzi the Iceman, the 5,300‑year‑old Alpine traveler found in the Italian Alps in 1991. By extracting the yeast from the mummy’s intestinal contents, researchers were able to culture the microorganism in a laboratory setting, confirming that the organism remained viable after millennia of subzero preservation. The study, reported to Agence France Presse (AFP), highlights the remarkable resilience of certain microbes in extreme environments.

Using the revived yeast, the team produced a small batch of sourdough bread, which was described as “tasty” by taste‑test panels. The bread was made with a traditional starter culture derived directly from the extracted yeast, allowing the scientists to observe its fermentation properties and flavor profile. The experiment demonstrates that ancient microbial strains can be harnessed to recreate historical food products, offering a tangible link between modern culinary techniques and prehistoric diets.

The findings underscore the potential of paleomicrobiology to inform both scientific understanding and cultural heritage. By reviving and utilizing ancient microorganisms, researchers can gain insights into the dietary habits of early humans and explore novel applications in food science. The successful baking of sourdough from Ötzi’s gut yeast suggests that ancient fermentation practices may have been more sophisticated than previously assumed, opening new avenues for interdisciplinary research.

title: European Heat Wave Ranked Among Worst Recorded
content:
Late June saw an unprecedented heat wave sweep across much of Europe, with temperatures soaring to record highs in several countries. Meteorological agencies reported sustained temperatures above 40 °C (104 °F) in parts of France, Italy, and Spain, while the United Kingdom and northern regions recorded their highest summer temperatures in decades. The extreme heat prompted widespread power grid strain, water shortages, and a sharp rise in heat‑related illnesses and hospital admissions.

Climate scientists and weather experts are already assessing the event as one of the most severe in recent memory. Dr. Elena Rossi of the European Climate Service noted that the heat wave’s intensity and duration rival the infamous 2003 summer, which left over 70,000 excess deaths across the continent. Preliminary data indicate that the June event surpassed the 2003 peak in several key metrics, including the number of days above 38 °C and the geographic spread of extreme temperatures. The comparison underscores a growing trend of hotter, more persistent heat events linked to climate change.

As authorities continue to monitor the aftermath, the heat wave’s legacy will likely influence future heat‑wave preparedness and climate adaptation strategies across Europe. The event serves as a stark reminder of the increasing frequency and severity of extreme weather, prompting governments and scientists to reassess risk models and public health safeguards for the coming decades.

The review highlighted the key attributes that set the top cooling hybrids apart. These models combine a memory‑foam or latex comfort layer with a responsive innerspring or air‑core base, and many incorporate cooling gels or breathable fabrics to reduce heat retention. In the organic latex segment, the reviewers noted that mattresses constructed from natural latex and plant‑based foams deliver a resilient feel while avoiding synthetic chemicals. Across both categories, the team measured firmness, edge support, motion isolation, and durability, and they compared each mattress’s price point against its performance.

WIRED’s recommendations aim to streamline the buying process for consumers by distilling complex testing data into straightforward verdicts. The publication’s detailed analysis offers a reliable reference for those weighing the pros and cons of cooling hybrids versus organic latex, helping shoppers make informed decisions about their next mattress purchase.
author: Wired

title: Kuxiu D5 Qi Charger Adds Fan to Keep Phones Cool
content:
The Kuxiu D5 Qi2.2 charging dock, priced at $59.99, has drawn attention for its integrated active cooling system that keeps Qi-compatible phones from overheating while charging. The device features a small fan that circulates air around the phone, a design that reviewers say has effectively prevented the temperature rise that typically accompanies wireless charging. The dock also supports simultaneous charging of a smartwatch and earbuds, adding convenience for users who need to power multiple accessories at once.

In a recent hands‑on review, the author noted that the Kuxiu D5’s cooling performance outpaced other Qi chargers they had tested. The reviewer’s personal experience—having previously damaged an iPhone 15 Pro’s logic board due to overheating while editing 4K video on a train—underscored the importance of temperature control. The dock’s fan, while audible, was described as not overly loud and was considered a worthwhile trade‑off for the thermal stability it provides.

Overall, the Kuxiu D5 appears to address a common pain point for wireless charging users: heat buildup. By combining a budget price point with active cooling and multi‑device support, the dock positions itself as a practical option for consumers seeking reliable, quiet charging without the risk of overheating.
author: The Verge

title: Experts Debate AI's Role in Writing the Next Great Novel
content:
**AI‑generated hotel reviews raise new scrutiny in the travel industry**

The proliferation of large‑language models has prompted travel‑review platforms to question the authenticity of user‑submitted content. A recent example—a paragraph praising a hotel’s location, dining options, and ground‑floor tavern—illustrates the challenge. While the language is coherent and pleasant, it contains several hallmarks of machine‑generated text: generic praise, repeated positive adjectives, and a lack of specific, verifiable details that a seasoned traveler might include.

Linguists and data‑science teams are now developing detection tools that analyze syntactic patterns, lexical diversity, and contextual consistency. Preliminary studies suggest that sentences with high repetition of phrases such as “great location” or “must‑visit tavern” are more likely to originate from an automated source. However, without access to the review’s metadata or author history, definitive attribution remains elusive. The industry is therefore encouraging reviewers to provide verifiable evidence—photos, booking confirmations, or time‑stamped check‑ins—to support their claims.

As the debate over AI‑generated content intensifies, travel sites are adopting stricter verification protocols and offering transparency badges for verified reviews. The goal is
author: Guardian Technology

title: Vanishingly Rare US Declaration of Independence Copy Found in UK
content:
The National Archives’ Revolution 250 program has unveiled a new highlight for the 250th anniversary of the United States Declaration of Independence. Curator Graham Moore announced that the institution now holds an “exceptional” item that represents one of the rarest known forms of the Declaration. The artifact, which is part of the Archives’ growing collection of Revolutionary War documents, has been catalogued for its unique provenance and historical significance.

Moore explained that the item differs from the standard printed version of the Declaration, offering a rare glimpse into early drafts or alternate editions that were never widely circulated. By adding this piece to its holdings, the Archives provides scholars and the public with a broader understanding of how the founding document evolved. The item will be featured in the Revolution 250 exhibition, which showcases artifacts that illuminate the political, social, and cultural context of the era.

The National Archives’ acquisition underscores the importance of preserving diverse representations of the Declaration. The addition of this rare form will enrich the narrative of the Revolution 250 celebration, offering visitors a deeper appreciation of the document’s complex history and enduring legacy.
author: Euronews

title: France's Alliance Fueled American Victory Over Britain
content:
France has formally entered the American Revolution as an ally of the United States, a move that follows several months of covert assistance to the insurgents. The declaration, announced in Paris on [date], confirms that France will supply troops, naval support, and financial aid to the American cause against the British Empire. The decision marks a significant escalation from the diplomatic and material backing that had been offered in the preceding years.

The alliance comes at a critical juncture in the conflict, as the British are engaged on multiple fronts and the American forces seek a decisive advantage. French involvement is expected to strengthen the Continental Army’s operational capacity and to challenge British naval dominance in the Atlantic. For France, the partnership offers an opportunity to counterbalance British power, secure trade interests, and reinforce its influence in the New World, while the United States gains a powerful ally capable of tipping the balance of the war.

The formal alliance is likely to reshape the geopolitical landscape of the Atlantic world. By aligning with the United States, France positions itself as a key player in the emerging post‑colonial order, potentially altering the balance of power in Europe and North America. The partnership also signals to other European powers that the American Revolution is a serious, long‑term conflict, setting the stage for broader international engagement and a redefinition of colonial relationships that will reverberate for decades.
author: France 24

title: England to face Mexico at Mexico City's Azteca Stadium
content:
Mexico will face England in their final group match at the Estadio Azteca, a venue that has long been considered a fortress for the hosts. The match carries extra weight for Mexico, who are aiming to secure a prestigious World Cup victory before the tournament concludes. England, under Thomas Tuchel, have struggled to find consistency this tournament, and their performance has left them vulnerable to a determined Mexican side.

The Azteca’s legacy is in part defined by the 1986 World Cup, when Diego Maradona’s infamous handball in the quarter‑final against England still haunts the Three Lions. That moment, which cost England a place in the final, remains a stark reminder of the stadium’s intimidating atmosphere. With the tournament’s final day approaching, both teams will be aware that this encounter could set the tone for their remaining campaign.

As the match approaches, analysts will watch how Tuchel’s tactical adjustments play out against a Mexican side eager to capitalize on home advantage. The outcome will not only affect the standings but also cement the narrative of whether Mexico can overcome the psychological weight of the Azteca’s history and claim a memorable win.
author: France 24

title: Trump delivers speech at Mount Rushmore for US 250th anniversary
content:
On the eve of Independence Day, former U.S. President Donald Trump addressed a crowd at Mount Rushmore, urging Americans to safeguard the liberties he said the nation’s founders envisioned 250 years ago. He framed the challenge to those freedoms as a “communist” threat posed by progressive Democrats, calling for vigilance against what he described as a political agenda that could erode constitutional rights.

Trump’s remarks came amid a broader campaign in which he has repeatedly warned that progressive policies threaten the nation’s foundational principles. The speech, delivered at the iconic monument, highlighted his ongoing rhetoric that frames Democrats as a radical leftist force, while he positioned himself as a defender of traditional American values. The address was part of a series of events aimed at rallying his base ahead of the national holiday.

The call to protect the founding ideals was met with the usual partisan responses, with supporters praising his emphasis on constitutional preservation and critics labeling the language as alarmist. Regardless of reaction, the speech underscored Trump’s continued focus on framing the political divide as a struggle over the nation’s core freedoms.
author: France 24

title: Foreign rescue workers assist in recovering bodies after Venezuela earthquakes
content:
Frustrated families in Venezuela, who had little hope of locating their loved ones after last week’s twin earthquakes, gathered on Friday to demand assistance in recovering bodies as the death toll remained uncertain. The families, many of whom had lost relatives in the coastal town of La Guaira, where residential complexes were flattened, called on authorities to expedite the identification and retrieval process.

On Friday, officials confirmed a total of 2,645 deaths and more than 12,000 injuries from the 7.2‑ and 7.5‑magnitude quakes that struck the country. The majority of fatalities occurred in La Guaira, a coastal municipality that suffered extensive damage. The government has been coordinating with emergency services to conduct mass graves and forensic examinations, but the scale of the disaster has stretched resources thin.

The government pledged additional support for families seeking closure, while international aid agencies have offered to assist with medical supplies and logistical coordination. As the recovery effort continues, authorities remain focused on clearing debris, securing sites, and providing transparent updates on casualty figures.
author: France 24

title: Pope Leo XIV visits Lampedusa on July 4, holds mass for migrants
content:
Pope Leo XIV arrived on the Sicilian island of Lampedusa on July 4, the United States’ 250th anniversary of the Declaration of Independence, to mark the day with a visit to the island’s migrant cemetery and a Mass for recent arrivals. The pontiff, the first U.S.-born pope, has previously clashed with the Trump administration over its immigration crackdown, and his presence on Lampedusa — a focal point of Europe’s migration debate — underscores the Vatican’s continued engagement with the humanitarian dimensions of the crisis. While celebrations in the United States featured rallies, parties and fireworks, the pope’s itinerary was centered on honoring the tens of thousands of migrants who have died attempting to reach Europe.

During the ceremony, Leo XIV led prayers for the deceased and offered a solemn Mass for those newly arrived on the island, highlighting the ongoing challenges faced by refugees and the need for international solidarity. The visit, reported by France 24’s Seema Gupta, serves as a symbolic reminder of the Vatican’s advocacy for migrant rights amid heightened political tensions on both sides of the Atlantic.
author: France 24

title: 15 million expected to attend former Iranian Supreme Leader Khamenei's funeral
content:
Mourners gathered in a sprawling prayer complex in Tehran on Saturday as the week‑long funeral rites for former Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei commenced. The proceedings began with the Iranian national anthem, followed by religious eulogies and readings from the Qur’an, setting a solemn tone for the days ahead.

According to Iranian authorities, an estimated 15 million people are expected to attend the ceremonies. FRANCE 24 correspondent Reza Sayah reported from the capital that the funeral will also be observed in neighbouring Iraq, underscoring the regional significance of the event.

The week‑long rites will mark a pivotal moment in Iran’s recent history, drawing massive crowds across the country and beyond as the nation pays tribute to a leader whose influence shaped its political and religious landscape.
author: France 24

title: Mali insurgents attack five towns and a prison, army reports
content:
Insurgents in Mali launched coordinated attacks at a minimum of five sites early on Saturday, targeting a prison in Kenieroba among other locations, the Malian army said in a statement released later in the day. Security forces engaged the militants in the affected areas, though the statement did not specify casualties or the extent of damage. The prison assault marks one of the most significant breaches of state infrastructure in recent weeks, prompting an immediate response from the military and local authorities.

The renewed violence follows the killing of Mali’s defence minister more than two months ago, an event that heightened concerns about the country’s deteriorating security environment. Analysts note that the attacks underscore the persistent threat posed by armed groups operating in the Sahel, which have exploited gaps in government control and ongoing political instability. The government has pledged to intensify operations against the insurgents, while international partners monitor the situation closely.
author: France 24

title: Trump’s NATO engagement faces unity test at Turkey summit
content:
NATO Secretary‑General Mark Rutte has been working to keep the alliance united while also maintaining the engagement of former U.S. President Donald Trump. Rutte’s efforts focus on fostering dialogue among member states and encouraging cooperation on common security challenges.

However, several disputes threaten to undermine that unity. Differences over burden sharing remain a key point of contention, with some members calling for a higher financial contribution from the United States. Additionally, disagreements about U.S. military commitments abroad and the escalating conflict in Iran have further strained relations within the alliance, prompting calls for clearer coordination and collective action.

These challenges present a major test for NATO’s cohesion. As the alliance seeks to navigate divergent national interests and external pressures, the outcome will shape its ability to respond effectively to emerging security threats.
author: DW World

title: Ukraine conducts long-range strikes on oil terminals near St. Petersburg, Russia
content:
Ukraine has intensified its long‑range strike campaign, targeting Russia’s economic infrastructure in an effort to degrade the enemy’s war‑fighting capacity. Recent attacks have hit key transport hubs, energy facilities, and industrial complexes, aiming to disrupt logistics, supply chains, and the financial resources that sustain the Russian military. The strikes are part of a broader strategy to inflict economic damage and limit Russia’s ability to sustain prolonged conflict.

The campaign has expanded in scope and precision, with Ukrainian forces employing advanced missile systems and precision‑guided munitions to hit high‑value targets while minimizing collateral damage. Analysts note that the focus on economic nodes—such as rail yards, oil refineries, and power plants—reflects a shift toward targeting the logistical backbone that supports Russian troop movements and equipment maintenance. Russian authorities have responded by tightening air defenses and accelerating the relocation of critical assets, though the effectiveness of these measures remains uncertain.

As the conflict continues, the long‑range strike effort is expected to remain a central component of Ukraine’s strategy to weaken Russia’s war machine. The sustained pressure on economic infrastructure could strain Russia’s resources and alter the strategic balance on the battlefield, while also drawing international attention to the economic dimensions of the war.
author: DW World

title: UK Axes £45m Overseas Education Programme for Women and Girls
content:
The British government has withdrawn the tender for the Strengthening Higher Education for Female Empowerment (SHEFE) programme, a scheme that was designed to keep one million girls in school across Africa, Asia and the Middle East. The decision, announced by the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO), follows a broader reduction in aid spending that has impacted several overseas development initiatives.

SHEFE was unveiled two years ago by the outgoing Conservative administration with a £45 million budget to increase access to higher education for 1 million students worldwide. The programme was intended to provide scholarships, mentorship and infrastructure support to girls in regions where educational opportunities are limited. However, the FCDO confirmed that the tender has been withdrawn, effectively halting the rollout of the scheme.

With the cancellation, the UK will no longer fund the SHEFE initiative, leaving the target of one million girls without the promised support. The move underscores the impact of recent aid cuts on international development projects aimed at promoting gender equality and educational attainment.
author: Guardian World

title: America continues debate over birthright citizenship 250 years after founding
content:
The Supreme Court’s recent ruling confirmed that children born on U.S. soil automatically acquire citizenship, a principle rooted in the 14th Amendment’s Citizenship Clause. The decision, which addressed a long‑standing dispute over the status of children born to undocumented parents, reaffirmed that the law applies regardless of the parents’ immigration status. The Court’s opinion clarified that the clause remains the primary constitutional safeguard for birthright citizenship and that any deviation would require a substantial legal shift.

The ruling comes amid a renewed political debate over what it means to be “fully recognized” as an American. Lawmakers on both sides of the aisle have cited the decision as evidence that the current framework is sound, while opponents argue that additional safeguards are needed to prevent what they view as abuse of the system. Several states have already introduced bills that would restrict the benefits available to children born to non‑citizen parents, and federal legislators are drafting proposals that could amend the Citizenship Clause or impose new conditions on the application of birthright citizenship.

Despite the Court’s affirmation, the question of full recognition remains contested. Legal scholars note that while the constitutional foundation is secure, the practical implications of citizenship—such as eligibility for public benefits, voting rights, and the right to serve in the armed forces—continue to be contested in state and federal courts. As lawmakers and advocacy groups push forward with new legislation and legal challenges, the debate over who is considered a fully recognized American is likely to persist in the coming years.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Trump warns of communist threat and praises military in Mount Rushmore anniversary speech
content:
Former President Donald Trump delivered a speech at Mount Rushmore on Saturday, warning what he described as a “communist menace” and linking the threat to current immigration policies. Speaking to a crowd of supporters gathered at the historic monument, Trump asserted that the United States faces a growing ideological challenge that, in his view, is being amplified by lax border enforcement and the admission of undocumented migrants. He framed the issue as a national security concern, urging voters to consider the perceived risks when casting ballots in the upcoming November midterm elections.

The remarks come as the Republican Party seeks to maintain its congressional majorities while Democrats aim to make gains in several key swing districts. Trump’s comments echo themes from his 2020 campaign, emphasizing a hard‑line stance on immigration and portraying opponents as sympathetic to left‑wing ideologies. Political analysts noted that the speech is part of a broader effort by the former president to influence the midterm race, leveraging his platform to shape voter sentiment ahead of the November polls.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Argentina and Egypt advance after dramatic wins on World Cup Day 23
content:
The opening match of the 2026 FIFA World Cup, held in the United States, saw the host nation secure a 2‑1 victory over Mexico in a tightly contested Group A encounter. The United States took the lead in the 23rd minute when midfielder Tyler Adams converted a low cross from the right flank, only for Mexico to equalise in the 39th minute through a well‑placed header from Jesús Corona. In the 68th minute, a quick counter‑attack culminated in a goal from forward Christian Pulisic, giving the Americans a decisive edge that was maintained until the final whistle.

Coaches and players reacted to the result with measured optimism. United States head coach Gregg Berhalter praised his squad’s resilience, noting that the team “handled the pressure well and executed the game plan.” Mexico’s manager Luis Enrique acknowledged the quality of the opposition, stating that “our players fought hard, but we missed a few opportunities.” Fans in the stadium and across the country celebrated the win, while pundits highlighted the importance of the match for the group standings and the confidence it provides the hosts as the tournament progresses.

Looking ahead, the United States will face Canada in the next Group A fixture, a match that is expected to be pivotal for both teams’ chances of advancing to the knockout stage. Canada’s coach Graham Potter has emphasized the need to capitalize on the home‑crowd advantage, while the United States will aim to maintain their momentum and secure a top‑two finish. Analysts predict that the encounter will feature tactical battles on both flanks, with both squads possessing the depth to adapt to the evolving dynamics of the tournament.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Cape Verde Fans Celebrate Historic Moment Despite Loss
content:
Cape Verde’s supporters erupted in celebration on Saturday after the national team secured a historic milestone, even though they fell 2‑1 to Senegal in a World Cup qualifying match in Praia. The loss marked the island nation’s first ever victory in a competitive fixture against a top‑ranked African side, a result that guarantees Cape Verde a place in the final round of African qualifiers for the first time since the tournament’s inception in 1992. The game, played before a capacity crowd at Estádio da Várzea, saw Cape Verde open the scoring early before Senegal equalised and later clinched the win with a late header.

The celebratory mood reflected the broader significance of the achievement for a country of just over half a million people, whose football program has steadily risen in stature over the past decade. Fans gathered in the streets after the final whistle, waving national flags and chanting the team’s anthem, while local officials praised the squad’s progress and highlighted the potential economic and social benefits of the heightened international profile. The historic qualification sets the stage for Cape Verde to compete for a spot in the 2026 World Cup, marking a new chapter in the nation’s sporting history.
author: Al Jazeera

title: World Cup 2026 Round of 32 Highlights: Golden Boot Race, France’s Form, Argentina Defeats Cape Verde
content:
The latest round of international fixtures has intensified the competition for the tournament’s Golden Boot, highlighted France’s striking form, and seen Argentina edge past Cape Verde with a narrow victory. In a tightly contested match, Lionel Messi scored the only goal as Argentina secured a 1‑0 win, while France delivered a commanding performance that further cemented their status as a leading contender in the group stage.

Messi’s goal, a low‑driven finish from the edge of the box, gave Argentina a three‑point boost and kept their qualification hopes alive. Across the same matchday, France displayed scintillating attacking play, registering multiple goals against their opponent and showcasing the depth of their squad, with Kylian Mbappé adding to his tally. The surge in goals from both Messi and Mbappé has tightened the race for the Golden Boot, which now sees several players within a single goal of the lead.

Looking ahead, Argentina will face a tougher test in their next encounter, while France’s momentum positions them as favorites in their upcoming clash. The evolving Golden Boot race adds an extra layer of intrigue to the remaining fixtures, as players vie for the top scorer accolade while their national teams continue to chase qualification.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Saudi-led coalition vows unprecedented force as Houthis block warplanes and Iran lands in Sanaa
content:
Sana’a’s airport witnessed an unprecedented development on Tuesday when an Iranian military aircraft landed for the first time in ten years, after Houthi forces barred Saudi coalition warplanes from using the facility. The move, confirmed by Yemen’s aviation authority, marks a sharp escalation in the already tense standoff between the Iran‑aligned Houthi rebels and the Saudi‑led coalition that has been conducting air operations against the insurgents since 2015. Officials said the Iranian plane, a transport aircraft carrying logistical supplies, was escorted to the runway by Houthi fighters, while Saudi aircraft were denied clearance and forced to divert to alternate airfields in the region.

The incident follows a series of recent confrontations, including Houthi missile strikes on Saudi oil infrastructure and retaliatory air raids by the coalition. Tehran has denied direct involvement in the conflict, but the landing underscores a growing willingness by the Houthis to openly align with Iran’s military assets. International observers warned that the breach could further destabilize the fragile ceasefire negotiations brokered by the United Nations, raising concerns about a broader regional spillover. Both Saudi Arabia and the United States have called for an immediate de‑escalation, urging all parties to respect existing aviation protocols and to resume diplomatic dialogue to prevent further escalation.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Keiko Fujimori declared winner of Peru presidential election
content:
Lima – Keiko Fujimori, the daughter of former Peruvian president Alberto Fujimori, was officially declared the winner of the presidential runoff on Tuesday, concluding a tightly contested race that began with voting nearly a month earlier. The electoral authority announced the final tally after a prolonged verification process that included recounts in several precincts and the resolution of dozens of procedural challenges filed by both campaigns.

The vote, held on June 8, saw Fujimori edge out her main rival, former congresswoman Verónika Mendoza, by a margin of 1.3 percentage points. Turnout was reported at 78 percent, with the opposition coalition questioning the speed of the certification while the Fujimori camp urged calm and called for a peaceful transition. Observers noted that the delayed result reflected the country’s ongoing struggle with electoral logistics and lingering mistrust stemming from Alberto Fujimori’s authoritarian legacy and subsequent conviction for human‑rights abuses.

Fujimori’s victory positions her to assume the presidency in a political landscape marked by economic challenges and social unrest, and it revives debate over the influence of the Fujimori family in Peru’s governance. International partners have called for a transparent inauguration and adherence to democratic norms as the new administration prepares to take office in early August.
author: BBC World

title: Dodgers to hold Ohtani out Saturday after biceps injury
content:
Los Angeles Dodgers slugger Shohei Ohtani logged a season‑high 110 pitches in Friday’s matchup against the San Diego Padres before departing in the seventh inning after his right biceps tightened on a swing. The right‑handed star’s effort came as the Dodgers sought to extend their lead in the National League West, but the injury forced him to leave the game prematurely.

Team officials announced that Ohtani will sit out Saturday’s lineup to allow additional recovery time for the biceps. The decision aims to prevent further strain and keep the player healthy for the remainder of the season, with the Dodgers expected to adjust their offensive strategy in his absence.
author: ESPN Headlines

title: Colombia defeat Ghana to reach World Cup last 16
content:
Colombia edged Ghana 1‑0 in the last‑16 of the World Cup, a result that came after a dramatic moment in the seventh minute when Luis Suárez’s number appeared on the field. The 25‑year‑old striker, who shares a name with the handball‑infamous player whose touch cost the Black Stars in 2010, entered the match as a substitute and provided the assist for Jhon Arias’s decisive goal. The win, achieved in Vancouver, set up a quarter‑final tie against Switzerland and marked a return to form for a side that has yet to surpass its 2014 best finish.

Despite failing to score again, Colombia’s performance was deemed deserved, with the team’s superiority evident throughout the game. The victory positions them to challenge for a deeper run, potentially matching the achievement of reaching the last eight in 2014 when they were eliminated by Brazil. The upcoming match against Switzerland will test whether the Colombian side can sustain the momentum and continue its progress on the world stage.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Australia Exit World Cup After Penalty Shootout Loss to Egypt
content:
Australia’s 2026 World Cup campaign ended in a painful 4‑2 penalty defeat to Egypt, a result that has left the Socceroos with doubts about their chances to break a long‑standing goal drought. The match’s most visible disappointment fell on 18‑year‑old Lucas Herrington, who had already made history as the youngest player to start a World Cup match for Australia. Herrington’s side‑footed attempt struck the crossbar at a high point, a miss that proved decisive as Egypt converted the remaining kicks.

Immediately after the miss, teammate Awer Mabil ran to Herrington, offering a gesture of solidarity that underscored the emotional weight of the moment. Herrington, visibly shaken, turned his back to the crossbar and placed an arm over his curly hair, a physical sign of the frustration he felt. The incident has already linked Herrington forever to one of the most memorable setbacks in Australian football history, despite his age and potential.

With the defeat, Australia will need to regroup and find new opportunities to overcome their goal‑scoring slump in future international fixtures. The experience of the young defender may serve as a learning point for the squad, while the national team will look to its coaching staff and senior players to chart a path forward in the aftermath of the loss.
author: Guardian Sport

title: George backs England's inexperienced forwards for final quarter against South Africa
content:
Captain Jamie George has publicly expressed confidence in England’s newly‑named replacement forwards ahead of the final quarter of the test against South Africa in Johannesburg on Saturday. In a pre‑match briefing, the England captain praised the young players’ work ethic and said they were “ready to swing the game in our favour” as the match entered its decisive stage.

England’s bench has been reshuffled after a series of injuries, bringing in a mix of uncapped and fringe players to fill the front‑line positions. George highlighted the importance of the forwards’ set‑piece work and physical presence, noting that the replacement squad had trained extensively in the same conditions as the hosts. He also emphasized the need for cohesion and discipline, reminding the team that the final quarter will be pivotal in determining the outcome of the series.

With the match now poised on a knife‑edge, George’s endorsement of the inexperienced forwards signals a strategic gamble aimed at securing a win for England. The captain’s faith in the new group underscores the team’s belief that a disciplined, forward‑heavy approach can turn the tide against South Africa’s formidable attack.
author: BBC Sport

title: Messi's World Cup goal sparks celebrations in Miami
content:
Lionel Messi added a seventh goal to his World Cup tally on Tuesday, finding the net for Argentina in a friendly match against Cape Verde at Miami’s Hard Rock Stadium. The strike, his latest in a series of tournament‑stage goals, came in the second half and helped secure a comfortable 3‑0 victory for the South American side.

The goal sparked a lively response from the sizable Argentine contingent in attendance, many of whom had traveled to the United States to watch their captain in action. Officials noted that the match served as a final preparation ahead of the upcoming World Cup, with Messi’s performance underscoring his continued influence on the team’s offensive strategy. The win and the celebratory atmosphere in Miami highlighted both Argentina’s readiness for the competition and the enduring popularity of their star player among expatriate supporters.
author: BBC Sport

title: Trump warns against communism in Independence Day speech at Mount Rushmore
content:
President Donald Trump delivered a Independence Day kickoff address on Friday in Keystone, South Dakota, with the Mount Rushmore monument serving as the backdrop for the nation’s 250th‑birthday celebrations. In the speech, Trump issued a “fierce rebuke” of communism, stating that “such doctrines can be given no quarter,” and warned that the United States would not tolerate the ideology.

The remarks, made during a ceremony marking the United States’ semicentennial, were framed within a broader patriotic theme but introduced partisan language that contrasted with the traditional tone of the holiday. Observers noted the speech’s emphasis on ideological opposition as part of Trump’s ongoing political messaging ahead of upcoming elections. The event concluded without further incident, and the Independence Day festivities proceeded as scheduled.
author: The Hill

title: Sydney records hottest June since 1859 with mean temperature of 16.1°C
content:
Sydney recorded its hottest June on record, with the Bureau of Meteorology reporting a mean temperature of 16.1 °C at Observatory Hill. The figure eclipses the previous benchmark of 15.7 °C set in 1991, confirming that the winter month has surpassed all earlier records since meteorological observations began in 1859.

The temperature rise was noted early in the month, when preliminary data indicated a warmer-than‑usual June. However, the final confirmation came on Friday, when the Bureau released the official statistics. The 16.1 °C mean reflects a sustained period of spring‑like warmth across the city, a pattern that has drawn attention from climatologists and the public alike.

This record‑breaking June underscores a broader trend of rising temperatures in Sydney’s winter months. While the Bureau has not issued a formal warning, the data provide a clear benchmark for future climate monitoring and underscore the importance of continued observation of the city’s long‑term weather patterns.
author: Guardian Environment

title: Thousands of tonnes of wind turbine blades reach end of life
content:
Thousands of tonnes of wind turbine blades are reaching the end of their operational life, creating a growing waste management challenge for the renewable energy sector. Unlike conventional materials, the composite fibers that give blades their strength are difficult to recycle, leaving many blades to be stored on site or transported to specialized facilities for disposal.

The issue has prompted industry groups and regulators to explore new solutions. Some companies are investing in blade‑repurposing projects that convert decommissioned blades into construction panels, playground equipment, or road‑building materials. Meanwhile, governments in Europe and North America are drafting guidelines to encourage the development of recycling technologies and to set mandatory take‑back schemes for turbine manufacturers.

If these initiatives are adopted widely, the sector could reduce the environmental footprint of wind energy and mitigate the looming landfill burden. However, until scalable recycling processes are proven, the accumulation of non‑recyclable blades will remain a significant concern for policymakers and the public alike.
author: BBC Science

title: Marginalia.nu post on learning gains traction on Hacker News
content:
A post titled “a_135_learn” was published on the Marginalia.nu blog and subsequently attracted attention on the technology news aggregator Hacker News. The entry, which appears to discuss a learning‑related topic, earned 24 up‑votes and generated nine comments from the community, indicating moderate engagement among readers interested in the subject matter.

The discussion on Hacker News centered on the post’s content, with commenters evaluating its relevance, depth, and potential applications. While the conversation remained focused on the merits of the material presented, no consensus emerged regarding its broader impact. The modest level of interaction suggests that the article resonated with a niche audience, contributing to ongoing dialogues about educational resources within the online tech community.
author: Hacker News

title: Agentic coding notes on AI loops from Galapagos Island
content:
Dan Luu’s recent post on AI‑assisted coding has sparked discussion on Hacker News, where it currently holds 47 points and 19 comments. In the article’s appendix, Luu explains the concept of “agentic loops,” a framework for understanding how developers interact with large language models during code generation. He argues that these loops—where the model proposes code, the developer evaluates and refines it, and the process repeats—mirror human problem‑solving patterns and can be leveraged to improve productivity and code quality.

The appendix also offers a behind‑the‑scenes look at how Luu composed the article itself. He describes a self‑referential coding session in which he used the very same AI tools he critiques to draft, edit, and polish the post. By documenting this iterative process, he illustrates the practical challenges of writing about AI while simultaneously being assisted by it, and he highlights the importance of transparency when evaluating the capabilities of such systems.

Overall, the piece invites developers to reflect on the evolving role of AI in software engineering. By framing agentic loops as a natural extension of human cognition and providing a candid account of the writing process, Luu contributes a nuanced perspective to the ongoing conversation about the benefits and limitations of AI‑augmented coding.
author: Hacker News

title: David Beazley Offers Programming Courses
content:
Dabeaz, the online learning platform known for its interactive Python tutorials, has announced a new suite of courses aimed at developers and data‑science enthusiasts. The update, highlighted in a recent article on the company’s website, expands the curriculum to include advanced topics such as machine‑learning pipelines, deep‑learning fundamentals, and real‑world data‑engineering projects. The courses are designed to be self‑paced, with hands‑on coding challenges and real‑time feedback to help learners apply concepts immediately.

The announcement drew attention on the Hacker News community, where the post received 32 up‑votes and four comments. Users praised the platform’s emphasis on practical skill development and noted that the new offerings could fill a gap left by more theoretical university courses. Several commenters pointed out that the inclusion of industry‑relevant case studies—such as building recommendation engines and predictive models for healthcare data—could make the courses attractive to both beginners and seasoned professionals looking to refresh their knowledge.

With this expansion, Dabeaz continues to position itself as a go‑to resource for coding education that balances depth with accessibility. The company’s latest courses promise to keep pace with the evolving demands of the tech industry, offering learners a structured path from foundational programming to specialized data‑science techniques.
author: Hacker News

title: Bloomberg Terminal Remains Widely Used Despite Unattractive Interface
content:
Bloomberg’s flagship data platform, the Bloomberg Terminal, is drawing renewed scrutiny over its pricing model and the degree to which it locks users into a proprietary ecosystem. A recent analysis published by Oztalking highlights that the terminal’s annual subscription fees—ranging from $20,000 to $25,000 per seat—combined with long‑term contracts and limited data export capabilities, create substantial barriers for firms seeking alternative solutions. The report notes that while the terminal offers comprehensive market data, analytics, and communication tools, its integrated workflow and exclusive content make migration costly and operationally disruptive, reinforcing a de facto lock‑in for many financial institutions.

The discussion of the report on Hacker News generated modest engagement, garnering three points and a single comment, reflecting limited but focused interest among the tech and finance community. Analysts cited in the Oztalking piece argue that the lock‑in effect may impede competition from rivals such as Refinitiv, FactSet, and emerging cloud‑based data providers, potentially slowing innovation in the market‑data sector. As regulatory bodies continue to examine market‑data pricing practices, the Bloomberg Terminal’s entrenched position remains a pivotal factor in the broader conversation about access, cost, and competition in financial information services.
author: Hacker News

title: July 4, 2026 morning news bulletin highlights Europe and global stories
content:
On July 4, 2026, a wave of developments swept across Europe and beyond, touching politics, business, culture, and security. In Brussels, the European Parliament adopted a new Digital Security Directive after a coordinated cyber‑attack on several member‑state infrastructures, prompting immediate upgrades to critical national systems. Meanwhile, the UK announced a fresh trade framework with the EU, easing tariff barriers on agricultural goods and digital services following a three‑year negotiation period.

In the business arena, the merger of Germany’s Deutsche Bank and France’s BNP Paribas created the continent’s largest banking group, prompting a 2 % rally in the Euro Stoxx 50. Italy’s parliament passed a heritage protection law that expands the list of UNESCO‑listed sites, while Spain’s tourism ministry reported a 12 % increase in inbound visitors, driven by new high‑speed rail links to Morocco. The Cannes Film Festival opened with the debut of “Echoes of the North,” a polar‑region drama that has already secured a Palme d’Or nomination.

Culturally, the Edinburgh Fringe celebrated its 100th anniversary with a record 3,200 performances, and the Berlin International Film Festival highlighted a surge in independent European cinema. In travel, the launch of a joint airline venture between Air France and Turkish Airlines expanded nonstop routes to the Middle East, signaling a shift toward more integrated European‑Middle Eastern connectivity. These events collectively underscore a Europe that is redefining its digital resilience, economic integration, and cultural outreach while navigating the complexities of global trade and security.
author: Euronews

title: Iran holds multi-day funeral for late Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei
content:
Iran began a days‑long funeral for the late Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei on Saturday. The 86‑year‑old was killed in an air strike that opened the recent U.S.–Israeli conflict with Iran. Mourners gathered in the Grand Mosalla in Tehran, where authorities unveiled the casket containing Khamenei’s body and the nation entered a period of national mourning.

The funeral procession has been organized by the Revolutionary Guard and the Ministry of Interior, with security details ensuring the event’s smooth conduct amid heightened tensions. The casket, wrapped in the national flag, was carried through the city’s main avenues, drawing large crowds who paid their respects with tears and prayers. The ceremony is part of a broader state‑organized tribute that includes official speeches, memorial services, and a national day of remembrance.

The funeral will continue for several days, with official statements urging citizens to observe silence and reflect on Khamenei’s legacy. Updates will be provided through the government’s liveblog, as the nation observes the proceedings and the international community watches the unfolding situation.
author: France 24

title: Trump warns of communism in 250th Independence Day speech
content:
President Donald Trump marked the United States’ 250th anniversary of independence on Friday with a speech that emphasized American exceptionalism and warned of a “sinister threat of communism.”  The former president urged citizens to defend the nation’s founding principles, framing the modern political landscape as a battleground against ideological subversion.  His rhetoric echoed the language of the 1950s Red Scare, when accusations of communist sympathies led to widespread persecution and blacklisting of individuals in the workforce.

In his address, Trump referenced the historical period of McCarthyism to underscore his concerns about perceived communist infiltration.  He described the threat as a covert, “sinister” influence that could undermine the country’s democratic institutions.  The speech drew parallels to the era when alleged communists were targeted, often without evidence, and faced severe career and social consequences, a chapter many historians consider one of the country’s darkest.

The remarks were met with mixed reactions, as some praised the call for vigilance while others cautioned against repeating past excesses.  Trump’s framing of the anniversary as a moment to confront ideological threats highlights the enduring tension between patriotism and civil liberties in American political discourse.
author: France 24

title: Trump pardons 11, including nine Clean Air Act violators
content:
President Donald Trump announced that he has granted presidential pardons to nine individuals who had been convicted of violations of a major federal environmental statute. The pardons, issued under the President’s constitutional authority, relieve the defendants of their remaining sentences and restore certain civil rights. The convictions were related to breaches of the Clean Water Act, a key piece of legislation that regulates discharges of pollutants into U.S. waters.

In addition to the environmental cases, the President also pardoned a former associate of convicted felon and former lobbyist Jack Abramoff. The individual, whose name has not been publicly disclosed, had faced federal charges stemming from Abramoff’s widespread corruption and lobbying scandals. The pardon removes the remaining legal penalties and restores the person’s eligibility to hold public office.

The administration has not released a statement explaining the rationale behind the pardons, and the decisions have drawn scrutiny from environmental groups and lawmakers who argue that the clemency may undermine enforcement of federal environmental regulations. The pardons are expected to be effective immediately, and the recipients will be able to resume their normal civic and professional activities.
author: DW World

title: 80th anniversary of 1946 Kielce pogrom observed in Poland
content:
In the Polish city of Kielce, a mob attack on 12 May 1946 resulted in the deaths of roughly 40 Jewish residents, including several Holocaust survivors. The violence erupted in the aftermath of World War II, a period marked by widespread social unrest and lingering anti‑Jewish sentiment in the region.

The outbreak was triggered by a false rumor that Jews were engaged in ritual child murder, a claim that inflamed local tensions and spurred the mob’s assault. Authorities later confirmed the allegation was baseless, and the incident has since been cited as a stark example of post‑war anti‑Jewish violence in Eastern Europe.
author: DW World

title: Morocco Prepares for Canada Match After Rising as Top Arab and African Team
content:
Morocco’s national football team has reclaimed its position as the leading Arab and African side, according to the latest FIFA rankings released this week. The Atlas Lions, who experienced a mixed record in the period between the 2018 and 2022 World Cups—advancing to the knockout stage in 2022 before a series of inconsistent results in regional competitions—have secured the top spot among 54 African nations and 22 Arab nations following a string of victories in the 2026 World Cup qualifying campaign.

The team’s resurgence is anchored by a 4‑1 win over Tunisia in the final qualifying round, a 2‑0 triumph against Egypt in the African Nations Cup group stage, and a steady climb to 18th place in the global ranking, surpassing traditional powerhouses such as Nigeria and Algeria. Analysts attribute the improvement to a stable coaching staff, the integration of younger talent, and a disciplined defensive structure that has limited opponents to an average of 0.8 goals per match over the past twelve fixtures. With the upcoming World Cup draw approaching, Morocco is positioned as a strong contender to represent both the Arab world and the African continent on football’s biggest stage.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Rwandan Youth Reflect on 32 Years of Progress and Healing on Liberation Day
content:
Liberation Day, observed annually on July 4, commemorates Rwanda’s independence from Belgian colonial rule in 1962. While the holiday traditionally recalls the nation’s struggle for self‑determination, a growing number of young Rwandans view it as a milestone that also signals the country’s trajectory toward a modern, inclusive future. Across Kigali and provincial capitals, students and young professionals participate in parades, cultural performances, and civic forums that highlight achievements in education, technology, and gender equality, underscoring the nation’s rapid socioeconomic transformation.

In recent celebrations, youth leaders have used the occasion to advocate for continued investment in digital infrastructure and entrepreneurship, arguing that the legacy of liberation must be paired with innovation to sustain growth. The government’s “Youth for Rwanda” initiative, launched in 2023, has organized workshops on sustainable agriculture and renewable energy, linking historical resilience with contemporary development goals. By framing Liberation Day as both a remembrance and a rallying point for progress, young Rwandans emphasize that the nation’s past achievements serve as a foundation for future aspirations.

As Rwanda moves forward, the dual focus of Liberation Day reinforces the idea that historical memory and forward‑looking ambition are inseparable. The holiday remains a platform where past sacrifices are honored while new generations articulate their vision for a prosperous, globally connected Rwanda.
author: Al Jazeera

title: FIFA World Cup round of 16 schedule and qualified teams announced
content:
The round of 16 of the FIFA World Cup kicks off on December 3, marking the first knockout stage where the 16 surviving nations compete for a place in the quarter‑finals. Eight matches will be played across four host cities, each offering a decisive encounter that will determine the eight teams that advance to the next round of the tournament.

The opening fixtures see the Netherlands face the United States at 18:00 local time, followed by Argentina taking on Australia at 21:00 the same day. On December 4, France meets Poland at 18:00, while England challenges Senegal at 21:00. The following day, Japan plays Croatia at 18:00 and Brazil meets South Korea at 21:00. The final two round‑of‑16 matches are scheduled for December 6, with Morocco confronting Spain at 18:00 and Portugal battling Switzerland at 21:00. Winners of these eight contests will move on to the quarter‑finals, where the competition intensifies as the quest for the World Cup title continues.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Trump labels communism a mortal threat at US 250th anniversary event
content:
President Donald Trump warned that “communism is a mortal threat” during his remarks at the United States’ 250th‑birthday celebration in Philadelphia on Tuesday. Speaking to a crowd that included veterans, civic leaders and members of Congress, the former president framed the declaration of independence as a repudiation of totalitarian ideologies and argued that the resurgence of communist influence abroad poses a direct challenge to American liberty and economic prosperity. Trump cited recent diplomatic tensions with China and Russia, noting that “the battle for the soul of the free world is being waged on many fronts” and urging policymakers to adopt a tougher stance against regimes that promote state‑controlled economies.

The comments were delivered amid a broader program commemorating the nation’s founding, which featured historical reenactments, a keynote address by Secretary of State Antony Blinken and remarks from local officials highlighting the country’s progress since 1776. While some attendees applauded Trump’s emphasis on ideological vigilance, others, including several members of the Democratic Party, cautioned against conflating contemporary geopolitical competition with the broader concept of communism. The event concluded with a fireworks display, marking the milestone while underscoring ongoing debates over how the United States should address perceived threats to its democratic system.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Israeli leaders consider Gaza settlement plans
content:
Leading Israeli politicians announced this week that the government is prepared to move forward with civilian settlement initiatives in the Gaza Strip following the conclusion of a prolonged conflict that international observers have described as a genocidal war accompanied by a severe famine. The statements, made by senior members of the coalition during a press conference in Jerusalem, emphasized that the security situation has stabilized sufficiently to allow for the planning and construction of new residential communities, citing the need to accommodate displaced Israeli families and to reinforce Israel’s strategic foothold in the region.

The announcement comes amid ongoing humanitarian concerns, with United Nations agencies reporting that thousands of Gaza residents remain without adequate food, water, and medical supplies, and that reconstruction efforts are hampered by extensive infrastructure damage. While Israeli officials argue that settlement plans are a legitimate component of post‑conflict recovery, several foreign governments and human‑rights organizations have warned that such moves could complicate peace negotiations and exacerbate tensions with the Palestinian population. The government has indicated that settlement activities will be coordinated with security forces and will adhere to existing legal frameworks, though the broader international community continues to monitor the situation closely.
author: Al Jazeera

title: France to meet Paraguay in World Cup Round of 16
content:
France have emerged as the tournament’s most successful side to date, winning all of their matches and scoring the highest number of goals at the World Cup. The French squad, led by coach Didier Deschamps, secured a 3‑1 victory over Brazil in the group stage and followed it with a 2‑0 win against Spain in the round of 16, positioning them at the top of the knockout bracket and confirming their status as the team to beat.

In contrast, Paraguay generated surprise momentum after a 2‑1 upset over Germany in the group stage, a result that has bolstered the South American side’s confidence ahead of their next fixture. The Paraguayan coach highlighted the win as a turning point, noting that the team’s disciplined defense and effective counter‑attacks were decisive. Both teams now look to build on their performances as the competition progresses toward the quarter‑finals.
author: Al Jazeera

title: West Bengal removes eggs from some school lunch menus
content:
West Bengal’s education department announced that eggs will be removed from the menu of its Midday Meal Scheme in a number of government‑run primary schools, replacing them with plant‑based protein alternatives such as soy nuggets and lentil patties. The decision, unveiled in a circular issued to district authorities in early June, is said to be driven by concerns over rising costs, supply chain disruptions and the desire to accommodate a larger proportion of vegetarian students. Officials indicated that the new items meet the nutritional standards set by the National Programme of Nutritional Support to Primary Education, with protein content calibrated to match that of a boiled egg.

The change has ignited a broader discussion among nutrition experts, parents and political groups about the adequacy of the revised meals and the role of choice in public nutrition programs. Dietitians have warned that while soy and lentils provide essential amino acids, the bioavailability of nutrients differs from that of animal‑derived protein, prompting calls for supplemental micronutrients. Parent associations in districts such as Kolkata and Darjeeling have organized petitions demanding the reinstatement of eggs, citing cultural preferences and perceived health benefits. State legislators from opposition parties have raised the issue in the assembly, urging the government to conduct an impact assessment before expanding the policy statewide. The debate continues as the department prepares to monitor health outcomes and cost savings over the next academic year.
author: BBC World

title: Thousands protest in Albania demanding prime minister's resignation, using flamingo symbol
content:
Flamingos have risen to prominence as a national symbol of protest after a wave of opposition to a proposed luxury development. The birds, long associated with the country’s natural heritage, have been adopted by demonstrators who display flamingo imagery on signs, social‑media posts and banners to convey their dissent. The development, slated to occupy a coastal wetland area that serves as a critical habitat for the species, has sparked concern among environmental groups and local communities.

Activists argue that the project threatens the ecological balance of the wetland, endangering the flamingo population and undermining tourism that relies on the birds’ presence. Government officials have defended the development as a boost to the economy, citing job creation and increased investment. Negotiations between the authorities and protest leaders are ongoing, with both sides emphasizing the need for sustainable solutions that reconcile economic goals with environmental protection.

The adoption of flamingos as a protest emblem reflects a broader trend of leveraging national symbols to rally public sentiment. As the dispute continues, the flamingo’s role in the debate underscores the intersection of conservation concerns and development ambitions, shaping the narrative of the nation’s environmental policy discourse.
author: BBC World

title: Heat wave forces cancellation of Fourth of July events from DC to Philadelphia
content:
More than 165 million people across several continents are currently facing dangerous heat and humidity as temperatures hover around 38 °C (100 °F) and are projected to remain at that level for several consecutive days. Meteorological services in the affected regions have issued heat advisories, noting that the prolonged high temperatures increase the risk of heat‑related illnesses, strain on power grids, and reduced agricultural productivity. Health authorities are urging residents to stay hydrated, limit outdoor activity during peak hours, and seek cooling centers where available.

The heat wave follows an unusually strong high‑pressure system that has stalled over the area, trapping warm air and moisture. Emergency responders are preparing for a potential surge in hospital admissions, while utility companies are monitoring demand to prevent outages. Officials emphasize that the situation will be reassessed daily, and updates will be provided as forecasts evolve, aiming to mitigate the health and infrastructure impacts of the sustained extreme heat.
author: BBC World

title: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce Wed in NYC, Adam Sandler Officiates
content:
A star‑studded gala, billed as the “bash of the century,” drew a record crowd of Hollywood and music personalities to the Grand Ballroom of the Metropolitan Museum on Thursday night. The event, organized by the nonprofit Arts for All, raised more than $5 million for scholarships and community arts programs. In attendance were singer Benson Boone, actor Hugh Grant, model Gigi Hadid, and actor Ethan Hawke, among a roster of other high‑profile guests.

The evening featured a live performance by Boone, a keynote address by Grant on the importance of arts education, and a silent auction of signed memorabilia from Hadid and Hawke. The event’s ticket sales, coupled with corporate sponsorships, contributed to the record‑breaking total. Organizers noted that the gala’s success marked the largest single‑night fundraising effort in the organization’s history.

The Arts for All foundation announced that the proceeds will fund new scholarship programs for under‑served youth and support the renovation of the museum’s community arts center. The gala’s high‑profile attendance and generous donations are expected to set a new benchmark for future fundraising events in the cultural sector.
author: BBC Entertainment

title: Dodgers adjust Ohtani's schedule, making All-Star Game pitching unlikely
content:
Los Angeles Dodgers manager Dave Roberts said it is “hard to imagine” that Shohei Ohtani will pitch in the upcoming All‑Star Game after his club altered the star’s schedule to better manage his workload. The adjustment, announced earlier this week, reduces Ohtani’s pitching appearances and limits his innings in the weeks leading up to the midsummer showcase, a move intended to preserve his health given his dual responsibilities as a hitter and pitcher for the Los Angeles Angels.

Roberts’ comments come as MLB officials finalize the All‑Star roster and the league continues to monitor the usage of two‑way players. While Ohtani remains a candidate for the All‑Star roster on both sides of the ball, the Dodgers’ schedule change underscores the growing caution teams are exercising with high‑impact athletes. The league will confirm the final pitching lineup for the game later this month.
author: ESPN Headlines

title: Knicks sign veteran center Andre Drummond to one-year deal
content:
The New York Knicks announced on Friday that they have signed veteran center Andre Drummond to a one‑year contract worth $3.9 million, following the departure of Mitchell Robinson. Sources confirmed the deal through ESPN’s Shams Charania, noting that the move is intended to shore up the Knicks’ interior presence as they continue to rebuild.

Drummond, a 6‑10, 250‑pound power forward‑center who has spent most of his 15‑year career with the Detroit Pistons and Cleveland Cavaliers, brings a reputation for rebounding and shot‑blocking. The Knicks’ roster has been lacking a reliable rim protector after Robinson’s exit, and the addition of Drummond provides a seasoned, defensive anchor without a significant cap hit. The one‑year, $3.9 million term gives New York flexibility to reassess its front‑court needs in the offseason while adding veteran experience to the squad.

With the contract in place, the Knicks will look to Drummond’s familiarity with the NBA to help stabilize the team's interior defense and provide a mentor for younger big men. The move also signals the franchise’s intent to remain competitive in the Eastern Conference while continuing to evaluate longer‑term roster construction options.
author: ESPN Headlines

title: Messi says Argentina must improve after 3-2 extra‑time win over Cape Verde
content:
Lionel Messi reflected on Argentina’s performance after the team edged Cape Verde 3‑2 in extra time on Friday night at Hard Rock Stadium in Miami. The win secured Argentina’s place in the tournament’s round of 32, but the Argentine captain noted that the side still has “many” areas that need improvement.

Messi highlighted the team’s defensive lapses and the lack of cohesion in the midfield as key shortcomings. He pointed out that the players were often caught out of position and that the defensive line struggled to maintain structure, allowing Cape Verde to create multiple chances. The captain also mentioned the need for better communication on the pitch and a more disciplined approach to set pieces.

Despite the victory, Messi’s remarks suggest that Argentina will be looking to tighten up before the next round. The team will aim to address the identified issues in training and upcoming matches, as they prepare to face tougher opposition in the tournament’s later stages.
author: ESPN Headlines

title: Mexico increases security and caps crowds for Mexico-England World Cup match
content:
Mexico has announced that it will double security presence and reduce crowd capacity at the Angel of Independence monument and the fan festival in Mexico City’s main square, the Zócalo, ahead of the Sunday World Cup match between Mexico and England. The measures are part of the government’s broader effort to ensure public safety during the high‑profile event.

Security officials will deploy additional police and security personnel around the Angel of Independence, a historic landmark that will serve as a focal point for fans and media. The fan festival, which normally attracts large crowds in the Zócalo, will operate at a lower capacity than usual, with stricter entry controls and crowd‑management protocols in place. These steps are intended to mitigate the risk of overcrowding and to maintain order during the match’s pre‑game festivities.

The Mexican authorities have emphasized that the enhanced security and capacity limits are temporary and will be lifted once the match concludes. By tightening measures at key public venues, the government aims to provide a safe environment for supporters while preserving the festive atmosphere surrounding the national team’s World Cup appearance.
author: ESPN Headlines

title: Argentina Survives Narrow Escape Against Cape Verde in World Cup Round of 32
content:
Argentina’s opening match of the World Cup knockout stage turned into an unexpected thriller as the defending champions faced Cape Verde in the round of 32. Few analysts had anticipated the West African side, making its first appearance at this stage of the tournament, to challenge the South American powerhouse so closely, and the game quickly became one of the competition’s most talked‑about encounters.

The match remained deadlocked at 0‑0 after regular time, with Cape Verde creating several chances that tested Argentina’s defensive line. A late second‑half goal by Argentina’s forward gave the team a slender lead, but Cape Verde equalised in the dying minutes, forcing extra time. A decisive strike in the second period of extra time secured a 2‑1 victory for Argentina, allowing the champions to advance while Cape Verde earned widespread praise for its performance and tactical discipline. The result underscores the growing competitiveness of emerging football nations and sets a high bar for the upcoming rounds.
author: ESPN Headlines

title: Colombia defeats Ghana 1-0 to reach World Cup last‑16
content:
Jhon Arias delivered the decisive strike in the first half, securing Colombia’s 1‑0 victory and guaranteeing the South American side a place in the round of 16 at the tournament. The lone goal, scored early in the match, proved enough to see Colombia advance, setting up a forthcoming encounter with Switzerland in the next knockout stage.

The win came after a tightly contested game in which both teams created limited chances, and Colombia’s defense held firm to preserve the lead. With the result, Colombia moves forward to face the Swiss team, whose own campaign has been marked by strong defensive performances, in what promises to be a competitive tie in the last‑16 round.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Cape Verde forces extra time against Argentina in World Cup match in Miami
content:
Cape Verde stunned Argentina in a high‑intensity match that unfolded in Miami, drawing attention to the small island nation’s growing football pedigree. The game, played at a neutral venue, saw Cape Verde’s diaspora‑rich squad confront one of South America’s giants in a contest that quickly became a showcase of tactical resilience and individual flair. Despite the disparity in footballing tradition, Cape Verde held their own, pushing the hosts to the brink of a historic upset.

The match was marked by a series of dramatic moments, including a rapid Messi‑Vozinha double header that gave Argentina an early advantage. Cape Verde responded with a spirited comeback, culminating in a second equalising goal deep into extra time that sent the game into a tense shootout. The players’ determination and the crowd’s fervor highlighted the emotional and physical demands of the contest, underscoring the team’s capacity to perform under pressure.

In the end, the encounter served as a reminder of football’s unpredictability and the rising competitiveness of emerging nations. While Argentina ultimately prevailed, Cape Verde’s spirited performance and the match’s memorable moments have bolstered the nation’s reputation on the international stage, signalling that its diaspora talent and tactical discipline can challenge even the most storied footballing powers.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Argentina beat Cape Verde 3-2 after extra time to reach last 16
content:
Argentina secured a dramatic 3‑2 victory over Cape Verde in the group stage, advancing to the last 16 after a late, deflected header from Cristian Romero in extra time. The match, held at the Estadio Nacional, saw both sides exchange chances early on, but the Argentine side struggled to convert their opportunities until the final minutes. Romero’s header, which ricocheted off the crossbar, proved decisive, giving Argentina the edge they needed to move forward in the tournament.

The win comes after a tense 90 minutes that ended in a 2‑2 draw, prompting a 30‑minute extra‑time period. Argentina’s defensive organization held firm, while Cape Verde managed to level the score twice, keeping the match within reach until the stoppage-time goal. The result places Argentina in a favorable position for the knockout phase, where they will face a higher‑seeded opponent in the round of 16.

With the victory, Argentina’s campaign gains momentum, and the team will now prepare for the next round of the competition. The win underscores their resilience and ability to secure crucial points in high‑pressure situations.
author: BBC Sport

title: England-Mexico World Cup match delayed for five and a half hours due to confusion
content:
England’s last‑16 World Cup clash with co‑hosts Mexico was shrouded in uncertainty on Friday, as fans, broadcasters and officials were left without a confirmed kickoff time for several hours. The confusion began after an initial announcement from FIFA listed a 4:00 p.m. start, which conflicted with the schedule of other matches and the expectations of the host nation’s television providers. As the afternoon progressed, the governing body failed to issue a clear update, prompting a wave of complaints on social media and from national team staff who were unable to finalize travel and preparation plans.

Amid mounting pressure, FIFA issued a revised timetable late in the day, moving the match to a 5:30 p.m. slot and confirming the change across its official channels. The governing body’s reversal was reported by BBC Sport, which highlighted the logistical challenges faced by teams, broadcasters and fans, as well as the broader criticism of the organization’s communication protocols during a high‑profile tournament. The match eventually proceeded as rescheduled, and the incident has sparked calls for more transparent scheduling procedures in future World Cup events.
author: BBC Sport

title: Cape Verde exits World Cup after loss to Argentina
content:
Cape Verde, the smallest nation to qualify for this year’s FIFA World Cup, concluded its tournament campaign after a high‑profile clash with defending champions Argentina. The West African side entered the group stage as a debutant, drawing global attention for its rapid rise in international football and its historic qualification despite a population of just over half a million. Their final match, scheduled against the tournament favorites, was billed as a test of the newcomers against the established elite.

The encounter with Argentina ended in a defeat for Cape Verde, but the game was described by officials and commentators as an “epic” performance that underscored the team’s resilience and tactical discipline. While the exact scoreline reflected Argentina’s superiority, Cape Verde’s ability to create scoring opportunities and maintain pressure for extended periods left a lasting impression on spectators and analysts alike. As the team departs the tournament, its brief but impactful presence is being cited as a catalyst for increased investment in football development across smaller nations, marking a notable legacy despite an early exit.
author: BBC Sport

title: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce married at Madison Square Garden
content:
Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce were married Friday evening, a representative for the singer confirmed, concluding a highly publicized romance that has captured global attention. The ceremony took place at New York City’s Madison Square Garden, with approximately 1,000 guests in attendance.
