title: Kyiv Mourns 30 Killed in Russian Attack, Rescuers Search for Survivors
content:
Rescuers in Kyiv continued clearing rubble on Friday, working to locate additional survivors after a Russian missile and drone strike the previous day killed at least 30 civilians. The city’s emergency services have been operating around the clock, with teams employing specialized equipment to sift through debris and assess structural damage.

In a solemn gesture, the Ukrainian flag was lowered to half mast across the capital to mark a day of mourning. The attack, which struck residential areas and critical infrastructure, has intensified international calls for accountability and increased the urgency of humanitarian aid efforts. Local authorities have coordinated with international partners to provide medical support and logistical assistance to the affected neighborhoods.

As the city mourns its losses, Kyiv’s residents and officials remain focused on recovery and resilience. The ongoing search for survivors underscores the broader humanitarian crisis unfolding in the region, while the collective mourning serves as a reminder of the conflict’s human cost.
author: France 24

title: Venezuela Earthquake Rescue Efforts Continue Amid Criticism of Response
content:
Rescuers have been sifting through rubble across Venezuela for eight days following two powerful earthquakes that struck the country, a search that is now yielding diminishing prospects of finding survivors. The twin tremors, which together have claimed more than 2,000 lives, have left extensive damage in multiple regions, prompting a massive, ongoing relief operation that continues to dig for any remaining victims amid increasingly slim odds of finding those still alive.  

Amid the disaster, Interim President Delcy Rodríguez dismissed accusations that the government’s response was delayed, rejecting criticism that officials acted too slowly in the aftermath. The administration has defended its actions while facing widespread scrutiny from domestic and international observers regarding the speed and coordination of emergency aid and recovery efforts.
author: France 24

title: Giorgia Melani loses judicial reform referendum as Italy's first female prime minister
content:
Giorgia Meloni became the first woman to head an Italian government on 25 September 2022, a milestone that resonated with many Italians who saw her rise from a disadvantaged Roman neighbourhood to the pinnacle of political power. Her election followed a coalition of right‑wing parties that secured a majority in the 2022 general election, positioning her as a central figure in Italy’s contemporary politics.

In March 2024, a nationwide referendum on proposed judicial reforms—an initiative championed by Meloni’s administration—was rejected by voters. The setback, seen by analysts as a blow to the perceived invincibility of her leadership, marks a turning point as her term draws to a close. The referendum’s outcome has prompted calls for a reassessment of her government’s agenda and raised questions about the future direction of Italy’s political landscape.

As the government enters its final months, the focus shifts to how Meloni will navigate the post‑referendum environment and what strategies she will employ to maintain stability. The outcome of this period will likely influence the political calculus ahead of the next general election and shape the trajectory of Italy’s governance in the coming years.
author: France 24

title: Spain defeat Austria 3-0 to reach World Cup last 16
content:
Spain, the reigning European champions, advanced to the World Cup round of 16 on Thursday with a 3‑0 victory over Austria. The win, achieved without reply, secured Spain’s place in the knockout stage and positioned them for a possible encounter with Cristiano Ronaldo’s Portugal in the next round.

The decisive result underscores Spain’s strong start to the tournament and sets up a high‑profile clash in the last‑16, where the two Iberian rivals could meet. Both teams will now prepare for the upcoming match, which promises to be a key fixture in the competition’s progression.
author: France 24

title: Bad Bunny gets first Latin American wax figure at Paris Musée Grévin
content:
Bad Bunny has added a new milestone to his already impressive résumé: a wax figure, modeled after his latest album *Debi Tirar Mas Photos*, has been unveiled at Paris’s Musée Grévin. The installation makes the Puerto Rican rapper the first Latin‑American artist to be represented in the famed French museum, a tribute that follows his recent Grammy wins and a string of sold‑out shows across Europe.

The unveiling coincides with Bad Bunny’s European tour, which includes headline concerts in Paris and Marseille. While performing, the artist has been seen proudly waving the Puerto Rican flag, underscoring his cultural pride amid international acclaim. The Musée Grévin exhibit, curated to reflect the aesthetic of his new record, offers fans a tangible celebration of his global impact and the growing recognition of Latin‑American talent on the world stage.
author: France 24

title: Trump visits Mount Rushmore for US 250th anniversary as LA hosts rival concert
content:
President Donald Trump inaugurated the United States’ 250th‑birthday weekend on Friday with a visit to Mount Rushmore, the iconic monument in South Dakota that many observers have long speculated he might want his own likeness added to its carved faces. The trip, part of a broader series of events marking the nation’s sesquicentennial, placed the former president at the historic site as part of a schedule that includes speeches and public appearances aimed at highlighting American heritage.

At the same time, a separate celebration unfolded in Los Angeles, where a concert hosted by Queen Latifah featured performances by country star Chris Stapleton and alternative rock group The Smashing Pumpkins. The event, described by France 24’s Rochelle Ferguson‑Bouyahi, offered a cultural counterpoint to the presidential itinerary, drawing a diverse audience to honor the milestone with music and entertainment. Both gatherings underscore the varied ways the nation is commemorating its 250th anniversary.
author: France 24

title: US Press Covers 250-Year Celebration Amid Climate, Sports, and Celebrity News
content:
The Fourth of July weekend has drawn a mix of patriotic reflection and global concern in the press. Across the United States, newspapers have highlighted the 250‑year milestone of the Declaration of Independence, noting the country’s historical achievements while also addressing contemporary challenges. The New York Times, for instance, has paired its celebration with a stark warning about climate change, reporting that Europe’s glaciers are retreating at an accelerated pace due to recent heatwaves.

Meanwhile, in the United Kingdom, the media has pivoted to sports, with a flurry of coverage surrounding the national team’s upcoming match against Mexico on Monday. Football columns and analysis pieces have dominated headlines, underscoring the public’s enthusiasm for the international fixture. In a separate cultural note, several entertainment outlets have reported that pop star Taylor Swift is celebrating her wedding over the weekend, adding a personal milestone to the week’s mix of news.

The convergence of national celebration, environmental alert, sporting anticipation, and celebrity news illustrates the breadth of topics that dominate the news cycle during a significant anniversary. As the United States marks its 250th year of independence, the press continues to balance historical commemoration with pressing global and cultural developments.
author: France 24

title: EU lawmaker probes Pegasus spyware after Greek ex-MP targeted
content:
Greek former parliamentarian Stelios Kouloglou has been identified as a target of the Pegasus spyware, according to a new analysis by Citizen Lab, the cybersecurity research group at the University of Toronto. Pegasus, developed by Israeli firm NSO Group, is a sophisticated tool that can infiltrate smartphones, harvest data, and covertly activate microphones and cameras. Citizen Lab’s investigation, which examined phone logs and metadata, found that Kouloglou’s device was compromised in a manner consistent with Pegasus deployment.

The analysis indicates that the intrusion likely occurred through a malicious link or app download, a common vector used by the spyware to bypass operating‑system security measures. While the report does not disclose the exact motive behind the attack, it highlights the broader trend of state‑level actors using Pegasus to monitor political figures and journalists. Kouloglou, who served in Greece’s parliament until 2020, has publicly expressed concerns about privacy violations and the potential for political misuse of such surveillance tools.

Citizen Lab’s findings add to a growing body of evidence that Pegasus is being used to target high‑profile individuals worldwide. The group urges governments and security agencies to strengthen mobile device defenses and to increase transparency around the use of spyware. As the investigation continues, the incident underscores the need for robust safeguards against covert digital surveillance.
author: Al Jazeera

title: UN warns El Niño may boost heatwaves, droughts and heavy rain
content:
The World Meteorological Organization (WMO) has issued a seasonal outlook indicating a heightened probability of heatwaves, droughts and heavy rainfall across several regions as the El Niño phenomenon intensifies during the coming months. The forecast, released in a joint statement with regional climate centers, notes that sea‑surface temperatures in the central and eastern Pacific are expected to remain above average, a condition that typically amplifies extreme weather patterns worldwide.

According to the WMO, the elevated risk will be most pronounced in parts of North America, South America, Southeast Asia and eastern Africa, where prolonged heat spikes could trigger record‑breaking temperatures and exacerbate existing water shortages. Simultaneously, the agency warns that the same atmospheric dynamics may generate intense convective storms, leading to flash floods and landslides in vulnerable coastal and riverine zones. The outlook underscores the need for preparedness measures, urging governments and disaster‑response agencies to activate early‑warning systems and reinforce water‑management strategies to mitigate the anticipated impacts.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Portugal Beats Croatia in Dramatic World Cup 2026 Match
content:
The opening round of the 2026 FIFA World Cup, hosted across the United States, Canada, and Mexico, kicked off with a dramatic 2‑1 victory for the United States over France. In the first half, a stunning long‑range strike by striker Christian Pulisic put the hosts ahead, but France answered with a quick goal from midfielder Aurélien Tchouaméni. The Americans sealed the win in the 78th minute when defender John Brooks converted a penalty after a controversial handball call. The match, played before a sell‑out crowd at MetLife Stadium, marked the United States’ first World Cup win on home soil since 1994.

Reactions from the coaching staffs and players were swift and measured. Head coach Gregg Berhalter praised the team’s resilience and tactical discipline, noting the importance of maintaining composure after the early French surge. French manager Didier Deschamps expressed disappointment but highlighted his squad’s ability to stay competitive, emphasizing that the loss will serve as a learning experience ahead of the knockout stages. Analysts in the press box underscored the tactical battle, with the United States employing a high‑pressing 4‑3‑3 that disrupted France’s build‑up play, while the French side struggled to find rhythm in the early phases of the game.

Looking ahead, the United States will face Uruguay in the group’s final match, a fixture that many expect to be a decisive encounter for the top spot. Uruguay’s coach Óscar Tabárez has called the team “prepared and focused,” citing their recent success in the Copa América. Meanwhile, France will travel to Mexico City to take on the host nation in a game that could set the tone for the group’s remaining fixtures. Both teams are expected to field their strongest line‑ups, with France looking to rebound from the early setback and Mexico aiming to capitalize on home‑field advantage. The next round of group matches promises to deliver further excitement as teams vie for a place in the round‑of‑16.

title: FIFA World Cup 2026 Round of 16 matches set for Friday
content:
Three crucial matches are set to decide the final three spots in the Round of 16 for the upcoming tournament, as Argentina, Australia, Cape Verde, Colombia, Egypt and Ghana head into a high‑stakes showdown. The fixtures, scheduled for the coming weekend, will see each nation battling for a place in the knockout phase, with the outcome determining the final composition of the elite group.

The competition follows a multi‑stage qualification process that has already seen several teams secure their positions. With the remaining slots now contested by the six listed teams, the matches carry significant weight: a victory could propel a side into the Round of 16, while a loss may end its campaign. The games are expected to be tightly contested, reflecting the quality of the squads and the high stakes involved.

As the matches unfold, the football world will watch to see which of the six teams will claim the final places in the Round of 16, setting the stage for the next phase of the tournament. The outcomes will shape the tournament’s narrative and determine the opponents for the teams that advance.

title: Four killed in Ukraine after Russia's deadliest attacks, five killed in Ukrainian border strikes
content:
At least five people were killed in separate attacks attributed to Ukrainian forces in Russia’s border regions, officials said on Monday. The incidents, which occurred in the Belgorod and Kursk oblasts over the past 48 hours, resulted in three fatalities in a residential area of Belgorod and two deaths in a small village near the Kursk frontier. Local authorities confirmed the casualties and reported that the attacks involved artillery strikes and drone incursions, though they did not disclose the extent of material damage.

Russian officials condemned the attacks as violations of international law and pledged to strengthen security measures along the border. The Kremlin’s spokesperson warned that Moscow would respond proportionally to any further aggression. The incidents add to a series of cross‑border incidents that have escalated in recent months amid the ongoing conflict between Russia and Ukraine, underscoring the heightened tension in the region.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Israel approves plan for 13 new West Bank settlements
content:
Palestinian officials have cautioned that a newly announced Israeli plan could further isolate East Jerusalem, a sector already under significant political and demographic pressure. The proposal, which involves extending municipal services and infrastructure to areas adjacent to the historic city, was presented by Israeli authorities as a measure to improve urban management. Palestinian representatives, however, contend that the initiative would deepen the separation of East Jerusalem from the rest of the West Bank, limiting residents’ access to services and undermining the city’s status in future negotiations.

In response, senior officials from the Palestinian Authority emphasized that the plan disregards the rights of the predominantly Arab population and could exacerbate tensions on the ground. They called on the international community to scrutinize the policy’s implications and urged diplomatic channels to address what they described as an attempt to unilaterally alter the city’s demographic balance. The debate over the proposal underscores the ongoing contestation over East Jerusalem’s governance and highlights the broader challenges facing any resolution to the Israeli‑Palestinian conflict.
author: Al Jazeera

title: US police confront Egypt soccer team at Dallas hotel
content:
U.S. police officers intervened in a dispute with members of Egypt’s national soccer team on Tuesday evening at a hotel in Dallas, after the players posed for photographs with a group of supporters gathered outside the lobby. The incident occurred while the team was in the city for a scheduled friendly match against the United States, and police reportedly moved in after receiving complaints that the gathering was obstructing traffic and creating a safety concern for other guests. Video footage released by local media showed officers separating the players from the crowd, leading to a brief verbal exchange before the team was escorted back into the hotel.

According to statements from the Dallas Police Department, officers acted in accordance with city ordinances governing public assembly and crowd control, emphasizing that their presence was intended to maintain order and protect both the athletes and the public. Representatives of the Egyptian Football Association said the players were merely engaging with fans and did not anticipate any law‑enforcement response, adding that no injuries were reported and that the team remained focused on the upcoming match. The hotel’s management confirmed that security protocols were reviewed after the incident but declined to comment on specific procedural changes.

The confrontation has prompted both the police department and the Egyptian federation to review their coordination procedures for future events involving international sports teams. No charges have been filed, and officials from both sides indicated that the matter will be resolved through internal discussions, with an emphasis on preventing similar occurrences during upcoming fixtures.
author: Al Jazeera

title: NASA launches robot mission to retrieve falling space telescope
content:
A NASA‑funded robotic spacecraft was launched Tuesday to intercept a de‑orbiting space telescope before it re‑enters Earth’s atmosphere. The vehicle, dubbed the Orbital Retrieval System (ORS), will rendezvous with the telescope in low‑Earth orbit, capture it using a deployable net, and then fire a set of thrusters to raise the combined mass into a stable, higher‑altitude orbit, averting the risk of the telescope burning up on re‑entry.

The mission, a joint effort between NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory and several commercial partners, is intended to demonstrate a reusable method for salvaging high‑value space assets and mitigating orbital debris. Engineers expect the ORS to complete the capture within a 48‑hour window and to perform the boost maneuver within a week, after which the telescope will be monitored for continued operation. Successful execution could pave the way for future retrievals of defunct satellites and telescopes, extending the functional lifespan of costly scientific instruments in orbit.

title: France reports 2,025 excess deaths during heatwave peak
content:
Forecasters across the continent have issued alerts indicating that extreme temperatures are expected to persist for the next several days. National meteorological services, including the European Centre for Medium‑Range Weather Forecasts and the African Centre for Meteorological Services, have upgraded heat warnings to the highest level for large swathes of the region.

The upcoming heatwave is projected to push daily maximum temperatures above 40 °C (104 °F) in many inland areas, with coastal zones likely to see lows remaining above 30 °C (86 °F) even at night. Models show the high‑pressure ridge responsible for the current heat will remain stationary, limiting the influx of cooler air masses. Authorities have urged residents to stay hydrated, limit outdoor activity during peak heat hours, and check on vulnerable populations. Health ministries in several countries have activated emergency response plans, and power utilities are preparing for increased demand on electricity grids.

The sustained extreme heat is expected to strain water resources, agricultural output, and public health services throughout the affected regions. Officials will continue to monitor atmospheric conditions and update advisories as new data become available, emphasizing the importance of preparedness as the heatwave progresses.

title: Portugal through to face Spain after VAR decision, Salah fit for Australia match
content:
The opening match of the World Cup on Friday saw Australia’s Socceroos face Egypt, a game that drew record-breaking viewership in the United States.  Fox Sports reported an average audience of 24.429 million viewers, making it the most-watched English‑language soccer broadcast in U.S. history, with a peak of 31.883 million at one point during the match.  Telemundo, carrying the Spanish‑language rights, logged 9.1 million viewers over the entire game window.

Australia’s coach, Tony Popovic, prepared his squad for both scenarios regarding Egyptian striker Mohamed Salah, noting that the team had trained for the possibility of Salah playing and for the alternative if he were absent.  “We have prepared for Salah playing, we’ve seen when he’s not on the pitch the players in those positions where he may play,” Popovic said, emphasizing the squad’s readiness to adapt to any lineup changes.

The match set a new benchmark for World Cup viewership in the U.S., underscoring the tournament’s growing popularity across both English and Spanish audiences.  As the tournament progresses, broadcasters and teams alike will continue to monitor and respond to the high engagement levels that define this global event.
author: Guardian Sport

title: UK Produces Multiple Elite Heavyweight Boxers
content:
The United Kingdom has emerged as a global hub for elite heavyweight boxing, producing champions such as Anthony Joshua, Tyson Fury, and Daniel Dubois in recent years. This resurgence has sparked interest in the factors behind Britain’s dominance in the sport’s most prestigious division. A combination of historical legacy, investment in grassroots programs, and strategic promotion of high-profile fights has created an environment conducive to nurturing world-class talent.  

The UK’s boxing ecosystem benefits from a deep-rooted cultural appreciation for the sport, bolstered by extensive media coverage and lucrative domestic and international events. Organizations like the British Boxing Board of Control have streamlined licensing and safety protocols, while private and public funding initiatives have expanded access to state-of-the-art training facilities. Additionally, the presence of charismatic, marketable fighters has drawn global attention, with British heavyweights frequently headlining major pay-per-view bouts. However, challenges persist, including competition from emerging boxing powers in the U.S., Ukraine, and Russia, as well as the physical and financial risks inherent in the sport.  

Looking ahead, the future of British heavyweight boxing hinges on sustaining investment in youth development and maintaining a balance between commercial appeal and athlete welfare. With a new generation of fighters entering the ring and evolving broadcasting opportunities, the division’s prominence appears secure, though its long-term success will depend on adapting to shifting global dynamics and ensuring a steady pipeline of competitive talent.

title: Forbes Reveals SNP Leadership Bid Impact
content:
The former deputy first minister of Scotland has revealed she was pressured to misrepresent her views on same-sex marriage during her political career, sparking renewed debate over transparency in public office. In a recent interview, she stated that senior figures within her party advised her to downplay her personal stance on the issue to avoid controversy ahead of legislative decisions. Her comments come amid ongoing discussions about LGBTQ+ rights in Scotland, where same-sex marriage has been legally recognized since 2014.  

The former official, whose tenure overlapped with key debates on equality legislation, described the advice as an attempt to align her public statements with broader political strategies. She emphasized that her personal support for marriage equality remained unchanged, but acknowledged the tension between individual beliefs and institutional expectations. A spokesperson for the Labour Party, which she previously represented, declined to comment directly but reiterated the party’s longstanding commitment to LGBTQ+ rights. Critics have called for greater accountability in how political leaders navigate such issues, while supporters argue the remarks highlight the challenges of balancing policy with personal ethics.  

This disclosure adds to a broader conversation about honesty in governance and the pressures faced by politicians in divisive cultural debates. As Scotland continues to address social policy reforms, the incident underscores the complexities of aligning personal convictions with public service obligations. The former deputy first minister’s account has prompted calls for transparency in political decision-making processes, particularly on matters central to equality and human rights.
author: BBC Politics

title: UK Delays Pledge to Tropical Forest Protection Fund
content:
The Brazil-led Tropical Forest Finance Facility (TFFF), introduced at COP30 as a pioneering mechanism to incentivize rainforest conservation, faces uncertainty after the United Kingdom delayed a pledged contribution, raising concerns over its viability. Designed to channel private and public funds into projects that protect tropical forests, the initiative aims to address deforestation by offering financial rewards for verified emissions reductions. However, the UK’s stalled commitment—initially announced as a £250 million investment—has left the fund short of critical startup capital, threatening its ability to attract additional donors and scale operations.  

Launched amid growing global urgency to curb climate change, the TFFF seeks to leverage innovative financing to preserve ecosystems that act as vital carbon sinks. Brazil, a key architect of the plan, emphasized the need for international collaboration to counter deforestation, particularly in the Amazon, which has seen increased degradation. The fund’s structure relies on upfront investments to guarantee returns for stakeholders, but its success hinges on securing initial pledges to build credibility. The UK’s hesitation has sparked broader questions about donor accountability and the political will to support climate finance, particularly as wealthier nations grapple with competing economic priorities.  

Without timely funding, the TFFF risks becoming a symbolic initiative rather than a transformative tool for forest protection. Experts warn that delays could deter other countries and investors from committing, undermining efforts to create a sustainable model for tropical conservation. As COP30’s momentum fades, the stalled pledge underscores the challenges of translating climate commitments into actionable support, with the Amazon and other critical ecosystems hanging in the balance.

title: Aberdeen Airport Security Staff Strike
content:
A planned strike by baggage screening staff at major UK airports is set to begin on Monday, with the Unite union warning of potential disruptions for travelers. The action, organized by the labor group, involves workers responsible for scanning luggage at security checkpoints, a critical component of airport operations. Unite has cited ongoing disputes over pay and working conditions as the primary drivers of the industrial action, which it claims reflects broader dissatisfaction among the workforce.  

The union emphasized that the strikes could cause "significant delays" during a key period for air travel, particularly as the UK approaches its summer peak. While the exact duration of the walkouts has not been specified, Unite has called for negotiations to address its demands, including improved wages and safer staffing levels. Airport authorities have urged passengers to arrive early and allow extra time for check-ins, while expressing hope for a swift resolution to minimize disruptions. The action follows similar strikes in 2022, highlighting recurring tensions between the sector and labor groups over operational and financial commitments.  

As the dispute unfolds, the impact on airlines and passengers remains a key concern, with potential ripple effects on flight schedules and connectivity. The government has not yet commented on the strike, but industry observers note that prolonged action could intensify pressure on airport management to reach a compromise. Unite has reiterated its commitment to protecting workers' rights, while acknowledging the need to balance labor demands with the operational needs of the aviation sector.

title: 18th Century Sailing Chart Secrets Unlocked
content:
A newly analyzed 18th-century navigational chart has revealed insights into the sophisticated yet distinct maritime practices of Red Sea and Gulf of Aden seafarers, shedding light on a regional navigation system that predated modern instrument-based methods. The paper scroll, crafted for sailors navigating these waters, demonstrates how communities in the region developed their own effective techniques to facilitate trade between India, Arabia, and the Horn of Africa during the age of sail. Researchers studying the artifact have uncovered evidence that these mariners relied on localized knowledge, such as coastal landmarks, seasonal currents, and oral traditions, rather than the abstract mathematical systems later adopted by European explorers.  

The chart, preserved for over two centuries, features detailed annotations and routes that reflect a deep understanding of regional geography and monsoon patterns, enabling precise voyages across complex waters. Unlike the standardized latitude and longitude methods emerging in the 18th century, this system was tailored to the specific needs of merchants and sailors, emphasizing practicality and adaptability. Historians suggest the scroll underscores the ingenuity of pre-colonial trade networks, which thrived on shared expertise and intercultural exchange long before the dominance of Western maritime technologies.  

This discovery challenges assumptions about the timeline of navigational innovation, highlighting the coexistence of diverse methods in global seafaring history. By decoding the chart’s strategies, scholars are reconstructing a more nuanced narrative of how non-European societies mastered oceanic travel, fostering economic and cultural connections across vast distances. The findings underscore the importance of preserving and studying historical artifacts to recognize the full scope of human maritime achievement.

title: EU Politicians Investigate Pegasus Spyware, Phone Incident Reported
content:
Citizen Lab, the cybersecurity research unit of the University of Toronto, has released new findings that expose a sophisticated cyber‑attack campaign targeting European institutions. The research, which details the methods and potential impact of the intrusion, was presented to the European Parliament where a member of the Parliament publicly condemned the operation as “a direct attack on the rule of law.”  

The findings outline how state‑aligned actors have deployed advanced malware to infiltrate critical systems across several EU member states, compromising sensitive data and threatening the integrity of public administration. Citizen Lab’s analysis shows the attackers’ use of zero‑day vulnerabilities and covert communication channels, underscoring the growing sophistication of cyber‑espionage and sabotage efforts aimed at undermining democratic governance.  

In response, European lawmakers are calling for tighter cybersecurity regulations and enhanced cooperation among member states to safeguard the rule of law. The new evidence is expected to influence policy discussions on digital resilience and the protection of critical infrastructure in the coming months.

title: Lisa Nandy Quits X Over Abuse and Misinformation Concerns
content:
The UK’s culture secretary, Lisa Nandy, announced that her department will cease all official use of the X platform, citing the site’s “now favours abuse and misinformation over meaningful debate.”  Nandy said the decision follows the earlier exit of the Department for Digital, Culture, Media and Sport, making the culture department the second UK government body to abandon the Elon Musk‑owned service.  

The secretary warned that X increasingly highlights and prioritises far‑right and racist content, which she argues fuels violence and division.  She added that the platform’s algorithmic amplification of such material undermines constructive public discourse and poses a risk to national cohesion.  As a result, the culture department will redirect its communications to alternative channels that better safeguard against abuse and misinformation.  

The move signals a growing governmental concern over the influence of extremist narratives on social media and underscores the need for public institutions to adopt safer, more reliable communication tools.
author: Guardian Technology

title: South Korea Faces Wealth Gap Amid AI Chip Boom
content:
South Korea’s booming semiconductor industry is once again at the centre of a headline‑making legal battle.  In a high‑profile divorce proceeding that returned to Seoul’s courts last month, the lawyers for the parties are arguing not only over the dissolution of a marriage but also the precise date to value shares in a single company.  The outcome could alter the worth of business magnate Chey Tae‑won’s holdings by billions of dollars.

The shares in question belong to the holding company that controls SK Hynix, one of the world’s leading manufacturers of memory chips that power artificial‑intelligence systems and a wide range of consumer electronics.  Because the valuation date determines how much the shares are worth at the time of the divorce decree, the court’s ruling will have a direct impact on the distribution of Chey’s assets.  The case has drawn attention from investors and industry observers, who are watching to see how the decision will affect the valuation of a company that underpins the global chip supply chain.

If the judges set a later valuation date, the shares could be worth significantly more, boosting Chey’s net worth and potentially altering the balance of power within South Korea’s tech‑dominated economy.  Conversely, an earlier date could reduce the value of the holdings, affecting not only the parties involved but also the broader market perception of SK Hynix’s financial position.  The ruling will therefore be closely scrutinised by both legal experts and market analysts as it could set a precedent for how corporate assets tied to rapidly evolving technology sectors are assessed in family‑law disputes.
author: Guardian Technology

title: Turkish comedian arrested for insulting Islam and President Erdogan
content:
Turkish comedian Deniz Göktaş, 32, was taken into custody at Istanbul Airport on Thursday after a stand‑up routine he posted on YouTube drew the attention of authorities. Police detained the performer on several charges, including publicly insulting religious values and defaming President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, offenses that are punishable under Turkey’s penal code.

The arrest follows a broader pattern of legal actions against public figures accused of violating laws that protect religious sentiment and the president’s reputation. Prosecutors have opened multiple investigations into Göktaş’s material, and the case is expected to proceed through the courts, where the comedian will face trial for the alleged offenses.
author: Euronews

title: Magnitude 6.2 earthquake strikes near Tobelo in North Maluku, Indonesia
content:
A shallow earthquake struck the North Maluku province of Indonesia on Tuesday, with its epicenter located about 58 kilometres west of the town of Tobelo. According to the Indonesian Meteorology, Climatology and Geophysical Agency (BMKG), the tremor originated at a depth of 120 metres beneath the seabed, a depth that limited its surface impact.

BMKG officials confirmed that the seismic event does not pose a tsunami risk, and no immediate damage or casualties have been reported. Residents in the affected area were advised to remain alert for aftershocks, while authorities continue to monitor the situation and provide updates as needed.

title: July 3, 2026 morning news bulletin highlights Europe and global stories
content:
On July 3, 2026, a series of developments across Europe and beyond captured headlines, ranging from political negotiations and economic shifts to cultural milestones and travel initiatives. At the European Union summit in Brussels, leaders agreed on a unified carbon‑pricing framework aimed at reducing emissions by 40 percent by 2035, while simultaneously endorsing a €150 billion fund to accelerate renewable‑energy projects in member states. In parallel, a major merger between two leading telecom operators—Telecom Italia and Spain’s Telefónica—received regulatory approval, creating the continent’s largest integrated communications network and prompting a modest rise in the Euro Stoxx 50 index.

Other notable events included a 6.2‑magnitude earthquake that struck the Abruzzo region of Italy, prompting emergency evacuations and a coordinated response from EU civil‑protection mechanisms; the Cannes Film Festival concluded with the Palme d’Or awarded to a collaborative Franco‑German documentary on climate migration. UNESCO announced the completion of a restoration program for the historic Alhambra palace in Granada, Spain, enhancing visitor access and preserving cultural heritage. Meanwhile, the inauguration of the Paris‑Lyon high‑speed rail line, cutting travel time to under two hours, was hailed as a milestone for sustainable tourism and regional connectivity. These stories collectively illustrate a day of significant policy action, economic consolidation, cultural celebration, and infrastructure progress shaping the European landscape.
author: Euronews

title: Israelis mark 1,000 days since Oct. 7 attack
content:
Thousands of people assembled in Tel Aviv on Monday to commemorate the 1,000‑day anniversary of the October 7, 2023 Hamas attack that sparked Israel’s war in Gaza. The gathering, held near the city’s central plaza, featured a solemn ceremony in which former hostages and relatives of victims took the stage to address the crowd, underscoring the lasting trauma and resilience of those directly affected by the assault that killed more than 1,200 Israelis and wounded thousands.

Speakers recounted personal experiences of captivity, loss and survival, urging continued support for families and a commitment to security. Their remarks were interwoven with references to the broader humanitarian and political challenges that have persisted since the conflict began, including ongoing reconstruction efforts and diplomatic negotiations. The event concluded with a moment of silence, reinforcing the collective resolve to remember the victims while confronting the enduring repercussions of the October 7 attack.
author: Euronews

title: Wildfire burns 900 hectares in France's Aude department
content:
A large wildfire has engulfed approximately 900 hectares in the Aude department of southern France, prompting an intensive response from local authorities and emergency services. The blaze, which began early this week, has spread rapidly across forested terrain, prompting the deployment of firefighting aircraft and ground crews to contain the flames and protect nearby settlements.

Firefighters have coordinated with the French Civil Protection and the regional fire brigade, using water‑dropping aircraft and ground hoses to suppress the fire. Evacuation orders have been issued for residents in the most affected villages, with many families already relocated to emergency shelters set up by local authorities. The incident has raised concerns about the increasing frequency of wildfires in the region, a trend linked to hotter, drier conditions.

Officials continue to monitor the situation and are working to secure the perimeter of the fire. As containment efforts progress, authorities remain focused on protecting human life and minimizing damage to property and natural resources.
author: Euronews

title: Switzerland beats Algeria 2-0 to reach World Cup 2026 last 16
content:
Switzerland secured a place in the last‑16 of the tournament after a disciplined 2‑0 win over Algeria in Vancouver. Breel Embolo opened the scoring in the 23rd minute, and Dan Ndoye added a second in the 57th, giving the Nati a comfortable advantage that held until the final whistle. The victory not only sent the Swiss side into the knockout phase but also marked the first time they have advanced past the group stage in a major international competition.

Algeria, who had shown early promise in the group, were unable to find a breakthrough against a resolute Swiss defence. Despite moments of attacking play, the Fennecs could not convert their chances, and the match ended in disappointment for the hosts. The result ends Algeria’s campaign and leaves Switzerland to prepare for their next opponent in the round of sixteen.
author: France 24

title: Portugal beat Croatia to reach next round of 2026 World Cup
content:
Portugal secured a dramatic 2‑1 victory over Croatia in the Round of 32 match staged in Toronto, overturning an early deficit to advance to the next stage of the tournament. The encounter, part of the knockout phase of the competition, saw Croatia take the lead in the opening minutes before the Portuguese side rallied in the second half.

Cristiano Ronaldo restored parity for Portugal by converting a penalty in the 78th minute, and the comeback was completed when Gonçalo Ramos netted a stoppage‑time winner in the 90+3 minute, sealing the 2‑1 scoreline. The late goal propelled Portugal into the Round of 16, while Croatia’s campaign ended with the loss.
author: France 24

title: France Sees 2,025 Excess Deaths in June Heatwave
content:
France recorded 2,025 excess deaths during the June 22‑28 heatwave, a rise of almost 30 percent compared with typical mortality levels, the health minister announced on Friday. The figure reflects the total number of deaths above the statistical baseline for that week across the country.

In the Paris region, the public health authority reported a 62 percent increase in deaths for the same period, indicating a disproportionate impact in the capital area. Officials attributed the surge to the extreme temperatures that persisted throughout the week and said monitoring of health outcomes will continue as authorities assess the broader effects of the heatwave.
author: France 24

title: France Supported American Revolution Early to Undermine Britain
content:
French support for the American Revolution began long before the Declaration of Independence was signed on July 4, 1776.  In the years leading up to the conflict, King Louis XVI recognized the rebellion in North America as a strategic chance to undermine Britain, France’s long‑standing rival, and to avenge earlier military defeats such as the loss of the French fleet at the Battle of the Saintes.  The French court, guided by Enlightenment thinkers and a growing sense of republicanism, began covertly supplying arms, money, and diplomatic backing to the American colonists.

The alliance that eventually crystallized was forged through a combination of European colonial rivalry and shared Enlightenment ideals.  French diplomats and military advisors, including the future Marquis de Lafayette, worked closely with American leaders to coordinate strategy and secure resources.  By 1778, formal military assistance was pledged, and France entered the war as an official ally, providing crucial naval support that turned the tide at key battles such as the Siege of Yorktown.  This partnership not only helped secure American independence but also reinforced France’s position as a dominant colonial power in the post‑war world.

In retrospect, the Franco‑American alliance exemplifies how ideological alignment and geopolitical competition can converge to reshape global politics.  The collaboration between the nascent United States and its “oldest ally” set a precedent for future international partnerships and underscored the enduring impact of Enlightenment thought on the pursuit of national sovereignty.

title: German AI Drones Deployed on Ukraine Front Line
content:
German defense firm Helsing has begun delivering its combat‑drone system to Ukrainian forces, a move that precedes a planned hand‑over to the German Bundeswehr later this year. The drones, designed for reconnaissance and precision strike missions, are part of a broader package of Western military aid aimed at bolstering Ukraine’s air‑ground capabilities amid ongoing hostilities. Deutsche Welle (DW) embedded with a Ukrainian combat unit to assess the drones’ operational performance on the front line, observing their integration into existing tactics and command structures.

During the field observation, DW reported that the Helsing drones were employed for real‑time intelligence gathering, target designation and limited loiter‑strike missions, with crews citing reliable communications and a relatively low logistical footprint. Ukrainian operators noted that the platforms enhanced situational awareness and allowed for rapid engagement of high‑value targets, while also reducing exposure of ground personnel. The assessment suggests that the drones are delivering measurable tactical benefits, a factor that may influence the Bundeswehr’s decision to adopt the system for its own reconnaissance and strike needs.
author: DW World

title: Canada Secures Pipeline Deal to Expand Oil Exports Beyond US
content:
Ottawa officials said the government’s plan to complete a new trans‑Canada oil pipeline will help lessen Canada’s economic reliance on the United States, a priority that has grown sharper as President Donald Trump’s trade policies have escalated tensions between the two neighbours. The project, which will link Alberta’s oil fields to the Pacific coast, is slated for completion by 2025 and is expected to increase export capacity by roughly 590,000 barrels per day, according to the Ministry of Natural Resources. By opening a direct route to Asian markets, the government argues the pipeline will diversify Canada’s trade portfolio and mitigate the impact of any further U.S. tariff measures.

The announcement comes amid ongoing disputes over steel, aluminum and other goods, which have prompted Canadian industry leaders to call for new avenues to sustain revenue streams. Ottawa has pledged to work with provincial authorities and Indigenous groups to address environmental and regulatory concerns, while also seeking private investment to fund the $15 billion project. If the pipeline proceeds as planned, it could generate up to 30,000 jobs during construction and contribute an estimated $5 billion annually to the national economy, providing a strategic buffer against future trade disruptions.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Iran Maps Ali Khamenei Funeral Processions July 3-9
content:
Iran’s top religious and political figure died earlier this week, prompting a series of state‑organized funeral processions that will run from July 3 to July 9 across major cities in Iran and Iraq. Government officials announced that the rites will begin in Tehran on July 3, move through Qom, Mashhad and other provincial capitals, and conclude with ceremonies in the Iraqi holy cities of Karbala and Najaf, reflecting the leader’s standing in the broader Shia community.

Security forces have been deployed to manage crowds expected to number in the millions, while broadcasters will provide live coverage of the events. The processions are intended to allow citizens to pay respects and to underscore the continuity of the Islamic Republic’s leadership structure. Observers note that the week‑long series of ceremonies will be closely monitored for any signs of political shift or public sentiment in the region.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Khamenei’s Coffin Readied for Seven-Day Funeral in Iran
content:
Iranian officials announced on Monday that the coffin of former Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei has been prepared for a state funeral scheduled to last seven days, beginning with a public viewing in Tehran’s Imam Reza Shrine. The body will lie in state from Tuesday to Thursday, allowing citizens to pay respects, before a series of religious and governmental ceremonies culminate in a burial at the shrine’s courtyard on the final day. Security forces have been deployed across major cities, and transportation networks are being adjusted to accommodate the expected influx of mourners.

The extended mourning period follows a tradition of multi‑day funerals for senior clerics and political figures in the Islamic Republic, designed to facilitate nationwide participation and to allow foreign dignitaries to attend scheduled rites. Iranian media have reported that high‑ranking officials, including President Ebrahim Raisi and members of the Guardian Council, will attend the final interment, while the Supreme Leader’s office has called for a period of national reflection. The funeral arrangements underscore the regime’s emphasis on ceremonial protocol and the role of religious symbolism in state affairs.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Switzerland defeats Algeria 2-0 to advance to World Cup Round of 16
content:
Switzerland have completed their first three matches of the 2026 FIFA World Cup without a defeat, keeping a perfect record as they advance to the next round. The Swiss side has managed to secure a combination of wins and draws, maintaining a points tally that places them at the top of their group.

In the upcoming fixture, Switzerland will face either Colombia or Ghana, depending on the final group standings. The result of the match will determine the opponent for the next stage of the tournament, with both potential opponents offering distinct tactical challenges. The Swiss squad will prepare to maintain their unbeaten streak as they aim to progress further in the competition.

The team’s continued success underscores their strong performance in the early stages of the tournament. With an unbeaten record and a clear path to the next round, Switzerland’s campaign remains a focal point for fans and analysts alike.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Delcy Rodriguez Blames Private Developers for 80% of Earthquake-Related Building Collapses
content:
Delcy Rodríguez, Venezuela’s vice president, said that private developers were responsible for roughly 80 percent of the structures that collapsed during the recent series of earthquakes that struck the country’s northern region. The assessment was made during a press briefing on Tuesday, where officials presented preliminary damage reports indicating that more than 1,200 buildings were rendered unsafe, with the majority located in privately owned residential and commercial complexes.

Government agencies have pledged to prioritize reconstruction efforts and to enforce stricter building‑code compliance for future projects. Authorities plan to launch a joint task force with municipal regulators and private‑sector representatives to audit existing structures, expedite repairs, and implement revised safety standards aimed at reducing vulnerability in subsequent seismic events. The initiative is expected to be funded through a combination of state resources and contributions from the developers whose properties were affected.
author: Al Jazeera

title: WHO warns Europe must prepare for permanent extreme summer heat
content:
The World Health Organization (WHO) has urged European governments to treat extreme summer heat as a public‑health crisis comparable to the winter flu. In a statement released this week, the agency warned that the record‑breaking temperatures experienced across the continent this summer are not an isolated event but part of a broader trend of increasingly frequent and intense heatwaves. WHO officials cited recent studies that link sustained high temperatures to higher rates of heat‑related illnesses, cardiovascular events, and mortality, especially among vulnerable populations such as the elderly, children, and those with pre‑existing conditions.

Experts from climate science and public‑health institutes highlighted that the current heatwave is a clear manifestation of long‑term climate change, with models projecting that such extreme temperatures will become the new norm rather than the exception. They called for a coordinated response that includes early warning systems, expanded access to cooling centers, public education campaigns on heat‑stroke prevention, and the integration of heat‑related risk assessments into national health‑care planning. The WHO also recommended that European health authorities adopt heat‑health action plans similar to those used for influenza outbreaks, ensuring timely resource allocation and surveillance.

In conclusion, the WHO’s call to “plan for heat like winter flu” underscores the urgent need for European policymakers to adopt proactive, evidence‑based strategies to mitigate the health impacts of rising temperatures. By embedding heat‑preparedness into public‑health infrastructure, the region can reduce the burden of heat‑related morbidity and mortality as climate change continues to intensify.
author: Al Jazeera

title: 40 people killed in Pakistan bus crash
content:
A passenger bus lost control and plunged into a rocky ravine near the border between Balochistan and Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, officials said on Thursday. The incident occurred on a remote stretch of the highway that links the two provinces, a route known for its narrow lanes and steep terrain. Authorities confirmed that the bus was traveling northbound from Quetta when it veered off the road and fell into a deep cleft.

Emergency responders were dispatched to the scene within hours, but the rugged terrain and lack of nearby medical facilities delayed rescue efforts. Preliminary reports indicate that several passengers were injured, with at least one fatality, though the exact numbers have not yet been released. The provincial transport department has launched an investigation into the cause of the crash, citing possible mechanical failure and driver fatigue as potential factors.

The incident has prompted a review of safety protocols on the Balochistan‑Khyber Pakhtunkhwa corridor, with officials urging stricter enforcement of speed limits and vehicle maintenance checks. The government has pledged to provide support to the victims’ families and to enhance road safety measures in the region.
author: Al Jazeera

title: Japanese Mayor Shoko Kawata Announces Maternity Leave
content:
Shoko Kawata, a 35‑year‑old professional, said she loves her job and is proud to be taking time off to have a baby after facing public criticism for her decision. In a recent interview, Kawata affirmed her commitment to both her career and her upcoming motherhood, emphasizing that the two are not mutually exclusive.

The criticism Kawata encountered reflects broader societal debates in Japan over work‑life balance and the utilization of legally mandated maternity leave. While Japanese labor law guarantees up to 14 weeks of leave for childbirth, cultural expectations have historically discouraged extended absences, contributing to a national dialogue about supporting families while maintaining productivity. Kawata’s remarks add a personal perspective to the ongoing discussion about how employers and the public view parental leave in the country.
author: BBC World

title: Iran begins public mourning for slain ayatollah, body to lie in state
content:
Iran’s Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei’s body will lie in state at Tehran’s Grand Mosalla starting Friday, ahead of a series of funeral events that will span several days. The ceremony will allow mourners to pay their respects in the nation’s largest mosque, a venue that has historically hosted the state funerals of prominent political figures.

The lying‑in‑state is part of a broader mourning schedule that includes a public procession, a state funeral service, and a final burial. Security officials have arranged for controlled access to the Mosalla, and the event is expected to draw large crowds from across the country. The schedule follows the traditional protocol for the burial of Iran’s highest religious and political leaders.

The funeral proceedings will conclude with Khamenei’s interment in a mausoleum that has been designated for former supreme leaders. The ceremonies are intended to honor his legacy and provide a national moment of reflection for Iran’s citizens.
author: BBC World

title: American Dream persists 250 years as confidence wanes
content:
The notion of the American Dream—a promise of prosperity and upward mobility through hard work—has been a cornerstone of U.S. identity since the era of the Founding Fathers. Yet recent surveys and economic indicators suggest that confidence in this ideal is diminishing. A 2023 Pew Research Center study found that only 35 % of Americans now believe that the dream is attainable, a decline from 44 % a decade earlier.

The erosion of faith appears linked to widening income inequality, escalating student debt, and a housing market that outpaces wage growth. Economists note that the median household income has stagnated for the past 15 years while the cost of living has surged. A report from the Economic Policy Institute highlighted that the top 1 % now hold 20 % of the nation’s wealth, leaving many middle‑class families with limited opportunities for advancement. Social scientists point to generational differences, with Gen Z and Millennials expressing less optimism about achieving the same level of economic mobility that previous generations enjoyed.

While the American Dream remains a powerful cultural narrative, the growing skepticism signals a shift in public perception. Policymakers and scholars are calling for reforms that address wage stagnation, affordable housing, and educational debt to restore the credibility of the promise that has long defined the United States.
author: BBC World

title: Taylor Swift's rumored wedding celebrations kick off with New York event
content:
Actress Lena Dunham, model Gigi Hadid and music producer Jack Antonoff were observed in formal attire near Madison Square Garden on Tuesday evening, according to multiple on‑lookers. The trio arrived together in a black sedan and were photographed walking along 7th Avenue before entering the venue’s main entrance, where security staff confirmed they were attending a private event hosted at the iconic arena. Dunham wore a floor‑length navy gown, Hadid opted for a sleek silver cocktail dress, and Antonson was dressed in a classic tuxedo, all reflecting the high‑profile nature of the occasion.

Their appearance coincides with Antonoff’s upcoming collaboration with several artists slated to debut at the venue later this month, though officials have not disclosed specific details about the gathering. The sighting underscores the frequent crossover between Hollywood, fashion and the music industry at major New York City venues, and no further statements have been released by the individuals or their representatives.
author: BBC World

title: Instagram ads in India linked to child sexual abuse material on Telegram
content:
Online advertisements have been discovered that employ graphic terms such as “rape” and “child video,” directing viewers to material hosted on the messaging platform Telegram. The ads, which appear across various web pages, contain hyperlinks that lead users to Telegram channels and groups where the referenced content is allegedly shared.

Authorities and digital‑platform regulators are examining the ads to determine whether they violate laws against the distribution of extremist or illegal material. Telegram has stated that it removes content that breaches its policies when reported, while law‑enforcement agencies are reportedly gathering evidence to identify the sources of the advertisements and assess any criminal liability. The investigation remains ongoing, with officials emphasizing the need for coordinated action to curb the spread of such illicit content online.
author: BBC World

title: BBC reports seized ships and shark fishermen as calm returns to Strait of Hormuz
content:
The British Broadcasting Corporation dispatched a reporting team to Bandar Abbas on Monday, marking the first time international journalists have been allowed onto the Iranian side of the Strait of Hormuz. The visit, part of a broader media initiative agreed with Tehran, follows months of diplomatic talks aimed at increasing transparency around the heavily trafficked waterway that links the Persian Gulf with the Gulf of Oman. Officials from the BBC said the team will cover port operations, naval activity and the daily lives of residents in the region, while Iranian authorities emphasized the trip as evidence of the country's willingness to engage with the global press.

The mission arrives amid heightened geopolitical tension over the strait, a chokepoint through which roughly a fifth of the world’s oil passes. Iran has previously restricted foreign media access, citing security concerns, and the opening of Bandar Abbas to the BBC is being watched closely by regional powers and commercial shipping interests. Observers note that the reporting could provide unprecedented insight into Iranian maritime capabilities and infrastructure, potentially influencing future negotiations on navigation rights and safety protocols in the strategic corridor.
author: BBC World

title: Switzerland Faces Algeria in World Cup 2026 Last 32
content:
The 2022 FIFA World Cup has spotlighted Switzerland’s 20-year-old forward Johan Manzambi as a standout performer, with three group-stage goals propelling him into the Golden Boot race. His tally places him among an elite group of players under 21 to score at a World Cup since 2002, joining Kylian Mbappé (2018) and Thomas Müller (2010) as the only others to surpass him in the century’s competitions. As Switzerland faces Algeria in a pivotal match, anticipation centers on whether Manzambi can sustain his form and challenge for the tournament’s top scorer award.  

Manzambi’s emergence has drawn comparisons to football legends who leveraged early success into legendary careers, though the Swiss prodigy remains focused on the immediate task of advancing his team. The Golden Boot competition remains wide open, with his three goals currently trailing leaders by a narrow margin. Analysts note that his ability to thrive under pressure—coupled with his team’s strategic emphasis on attacking play—could define Switzerland’s World Cup trajectory. With the group stage nearing its conclusion, every goal carries added weight in shaping both individual accolades and national ambitions.  

The match against Algeria, set for 8 pm local time (1 pm AEST, 4 am BST, 11 pm EDT), represents a critical juncture for Manzambi and his team. While the pressure to replicate past stars’ feats is implicit, his performance underscores the unpredictable nature of the World Cup, where young talents can redefine global football’s landscape. As the tournament progresses, Manzambi’s journey—whether as a Golden Boot contender or a catalyst for Swiss success—will remain a focal point for fans and analysts alike.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Portugal Advances to World Cup Last 16
content:
Portugal edged Croatia 2-1 in a tense World Cup last-16 clash marked by drama, controversy, and emotional farewells, with four goals disallowed across the match—including a last-second denied equalizer that ended Croatia’s hopes. The decisive moment came when Gonçalo Ramos converted Rafael Leão’s cross in the 61st minute, sparking a wave of relief among Portugal’s players and fans. The match, however, was defined by its relentless ebb and flow, as both teams traded momentum amid a backdrop of refereeing decisions that shaped the outcome.  

The contest featured a poignant farewell for Luka Modrić, who, at 40, was forced off injured in the second half, signaling the likely end of his World Cup career. Cristiano Ronaldo, meanwhile, extended his own legacy by scoring in what could be his final tournament, though his influence was overshadowed by younger teammates. The match’s chaotic nature was underscored by four disallowed goals, including a 98th-minute strike by Croatia’s Josko Gvardiol that would have forced extra time. Despite Ronaldo being named the game’s “player of the match,” the narrative shifted to Portugal’s collective resilience, with Ramos emerging as a key figure in their progression.  

The match highlighted the unpredictable nature of World Cup football, where high stakes and high drama collide. Portugal’s advancement to the next round was secured not by star power alone, but by composure in critical moments. Croatia’s exit, meanwhile, was tinged with frustration, their tactical adjustments and late chances undone by officiating decisions. As the tournament continues, the contest will be remembered as a classic example of the emotional and physical toll of international football, where legacy and heartbreak coexist.
author: Guardian Sport

title: Portugal Advances to Last 16
content:
Portugal advanced to the round of 16 with a 2-1 victory over Croatia in a turbulent match at Toronto’s BMO Field, securing a clash with Spain after a dramatic second-half encounter. Goals from Cristiano Ronaldo and Gonçalo Ramos proved decisive for Portugal, who overcame a spirited Croatian side led by Luka Modrić. The result sets up a highly anticipated Iberian derby against Spain, the reigning European champions, as both teams vie for a place in the quarterfinals.  

The match, played in the United States as part of the tournament’s transatlantic leg, saw Portugal dominate possession but struggle to break down a resilient Croatian defense in the first half. Ronaldo opened the scoring in the 58th minute with a clinical header, before Ramos sealed the win in the 83rd minute with a composed finish following a counterattack. Croatia responded with a late goal from Josko Gvardiol, but Portugal’s defense held firm under pressure. The second half featured multiple substitutions and erratic play, reflecting the physical and tactical intensity of the contest.  

With Portugal now poised to face Spain, the stage is set for a rematch of the 2012 European Championship final, where Spain defeated Portugal in a historic encounter. Ronaldo, who has been a consistent force for his nation, will look to lead his team against a Spanish side aiming to reclaim their continental supremacy. The clash promises to be a pivotal moment in the tournament, with both teams carrying the weight of their storied rivalries into the next round.
author: BBC Sport

title: Former Special Counsel Jack Smith Criticizes Trump Administration
content:
Former special counsel Jack Smith has warned that the United States is confronting an “attack on the rule of law” amid the Trump administration, expressing deep concern over the integrity of future elections. Smith, who was appointed to prosecute former President Donald Trump after the first term, said the current administration is weaponizing the Justice Department to further political ends.

In his remarks, Smith highlighted the erosion of impartial legal processes and the potential for partisan interference in electoral oversight. He accused the administration of using the Department of Justice as a tool to advance its agenda, thereby undermining public confidence in the electoral system. Smith’s statements come as the DOJ continues to investigate a range of high‑profile cases tied to the former president.

The warning underscores ongoing tensions between the executive branch and the judiciary. If the concerns voiced by Smith materialize, they could prompt calls for reforms to safeguard the independence of the Justice Department and preserve the integrity of the electoral process.
